findings.title: Needs you is one 51-row inbox with ~26 different verbs; "Show all" unrolls it in place
findings.now: Card head "Needs you 51" with text tabs "All · To approve 8 · Clients 8 · Late 7"; five rows at rest, "Show all 51" expands every row inside the card (page grows to 4,300px). The 51 rows mix decisions (Approve a bill, Agree to more time) with standing reminders that are not decisions: "11 compliance items to do · Design", "16 compliance items to do · Execution", "Save the brief of the meeting with Kevin", "Write up the meeting with Priya", "Start the project · When work begins on site", "Contract · The signed agreement · Add", "Invite the client", "Electrical & plumbing waits on the plumber · Open". Row verbs seen: Publish, Review, Approve, Agree, Answer, Start, Pay, Send, Remind, Record the refund, Confirm, Change it, Reply, Open, Revise, Call, Assign, Mark done, Write up, Move the schedule, Add a contractor, Mark delivered, Draft it, Share, Add, Invite. The chip counts (8 + 8 + 7 = 23) never add up to the head's 51, so "All" holds 28 rows no chip names.
findings.why: A studio owner opening the app sees "51 things need you" — a wall. The few real decisions (approve a bill, answer a client) are buried among project housekeeping that belongs on each project. Twenty-six verbs mean every row has to be read before it can be acted on.
findings.proposal: Rename the card "Needs your attention" (see 1-02). Keep ONLY decisions and people waiting on the studio: Approvals (bills, POs, claims, more-time asks, quotes, price-book items), Clients waiting (messages, marks, declines), Overdue money. Move the standing project checklist rows (compliance items, "Save the brief", "Write up the meeting", "Start the project", "Contract · Add", "Invite the client", contractor gaps, schedule shares) to each project's own Needs you — the Dashboard shows one roll-up row per project ("HDB 5-Room — Benjamin Han · 6 things to set up · Open"). Show 5 rows; "See all 23" opens the full list in the house Drawer (the Review pane's frame) instead of growing the card. Chips become "All · Approvals · Clients · Overdue" and only appear when there are 8+ rows.

findings.title: One idea, eight names: Needs you / need you / Needs attention / Needs my review / To do / To approve / Needs your OK / Waiting on you
findings.now: Dashboard card "Needs you 51" and greeting "51 things need you" (lib/dashboard/frame.ts:59,67); project Overview "Needs you" + group "Needs your OK"; Projects listing tile and scope "Needs attention" (components/projects/scopes.ts, rail aria "Projects (3 need attention)"); Projects listing "Needs my review" (lib/projects/queries.ts:43); Company › Finance lands on "To do" with a "To approve" group; Dashboard chip "To approve"; Company panel "4 to approve" / "1 awaiting" / "1 proposed"; tickets "Waiting on you"; empty "Nothing waits on you" / "You’re all caught up".
findings.why: The owner's own example. A studio learns one word for "this is waiting for me" and should find it on every page. Today each module invented its own, and "Needs you 51" reads as a fragment, not a heading.
findings.proposal: One vocabulary: the heading is "Needs your attention" (Dashboard card, project Overview card, Finance landing tab — rename "To do"), the scope pill on Projects stays "Needs attention" (same root); the approval group is "Approvals" everywhere (Dashboard chip, Finance group, Company panel pill "4 to approve" → "4 approvals"; "1 awaiting" → "1 approval"; "1 proposed" → "1 approval"); "Needs my review" → "Approvals"; "Needs your OK" → "Approvals"; the greeting's "51 things need you" is dropped (see 1-18); the empty state everywhere "You’re all caught up".

findings.title: The same approvals show in six places with three different numbers (8, 6, 1+1+4)
findings.now: Dashboard chip "To approve 8"; Tasks page banner "8 approvals wait for you on the Dashboard · Open Dashboard" (components/tasks/approvals-line.tsx:19); the rail's Company item wears a red "6"; the Company panel rows say "1 awaiting" (Templates), "1 proposed" (Price book), "4 to approve" (Finance); the bell's Notices repeat each approval with its own Approve / Send back buttons ("Bright Spark Electrical’s bill EL-2207 needs your OK before it is paid · Approve"); the project tab strip carries its own red counts (Money 6).
findings.why: A count that differs between the rail (6) and the Dashboard (8) for the same work makes a user distrust both; acting on an approval from the bell, the Dashboard and Finance means three ways to do one thing and three places to check it is done.
findings.proposal: One home for approvals: the Dashboard's "Approvals" group. Remove the Tasks banner (Tasks is for tasks). The rail's Company item drops its badge; the Company panel rows keep a grey count only ("4 approvals"). Bell rows for approvals keep their sentence but lose their inline buttons — a press opens the Dashboard's Review pane on that row (`?review=<key>`). Finance › To do lists the same rows (already the same source).

findings.title: Six red number badges on the rail at rest, each meaning something different
findings.now: At rest the collapsed rail shows red badges on Tasks "1" (my overdue), Projects "3" (need attention), Leads "2" (unseen new), Company "6" (approvals), Messages "1" (unread), Notifications "16" (unread) — plus the AI-credits ring. Same red, same size, six meanings.
findings.why: Red badges everywhere train people to ignore them. Only the bell's count is truly "unread"; the rest repeat the Dashboard's Needs you, which is the front door.
findings.proposal: Keep a red count only on Notifications (unread) and Messages (unread client messages). Tasks keeps its count only when something of mine is overdue — as a red dot, no number. Drop the Projects, Leads and Company badges (they are the Dashboard's rows). Same rule on the phone dock and More sheet (`badgeHref` / `countOf`).

findings.route: /dashboard · Review pane · bell · Maison AI answers
findings.title: An approval row shows a different amount than its own pane: "S$ 39" vs "S$38.50", "S$ 5,530" vs "S$5,529.57"
findings.now: Dashboard rows round to the dollar with a space ("S$ 5,530", "S$ 39", "S$ 6,104", "−S$ 545") via moneyCard; the Review pane for the same PO says "Amount S$5,529.57"; the bell says "Germaine logged an expense of S$38.50" for the row the Dashboard shows as "S$ 39"; Pulse says "S$ 34.8K … S$ 34.2K past due · 2 invoices" while Maison AI's answer to "How much do clients owe us?" says "Owed to you · S$34,802.98 / 3 invoices not paid in full · S$34,154.98 overdue". Four formats (S$ 39 · S$38.50 · S$ 34.8K · −S$ 545) on one page.
findings.why: Approving money is the one place an owner checks the figure to the cent. Seeing S$ 39 on the row and S$38.50 elsewhere looks like an error. "2 invoices" vs "3 invoices" for the same debt reads as a wrong number.
findings.proposal: One money rule: anything you approve, pay or confirm shows the exact amount "S$5,529.57" (no space, cents) — rows, pane, bell alike; only Pulse figures abbreviate ("S$34.8K"). Negative as "–S$545.00 credit" is wrong for a VO that takes money off: say "S$545.00 less" or show it unsigned under "Saves". Pulse and the answer card use one count ("3 invoices · S$34,154.98 overdue").

findings.title: Tasks shows nine controls and a purple banner before the first task
findings.now: Header: filled "Add Task" + ⋮. Then a purple banner "8 approvals wait for you on the Dashboard · Open Dashboard". Then: scope pill "All Tasks (48) ▾" (All Tasks · My Tasks · Unassigned · Studio Tasks), a segmented "All · Leads · Projects", three outlined to-do chips "Overdue · 6", "Due today · 6", "Unassigned · 15", a search box, Filters and Column settings. findings.proposal: Remove the banner (1-03). Scope pill: "All tasks · My tasks · General tasks" (drop Unassigned — the chip keeps it). Fold "All · Leads · Projects" into Filters (its Lead / Project tabs already exist). Keep the same three chips in every scope: "Overdue 6 · Today 6 · Unassigned 15". After: [All tasks (48) ▾] [Overdue 6] [Today 6] [Unassigned 15] ……… [Search] [Filters] [Columns].

findings.title: Every task row repeats "OPEN", "+ Add Tags" and "Assign" — 63 purple text actions on one screen
findings.now: Each row: an outlined "OPEN" tag (every row on an open list), a purple "+ Add Tags" link in the last column, a purple "Assign" link with an icon on unassigned rows, avatar "+" buttons, an underlined due date; hover adds "Edit" + ⋮ over the date ("Thu, 10 Sep ’26 [Edit] ⋮" hides the time). Tags: show the tags when a task has them, else an empty cell; "Add tags" moves to the row ⋮ and the panel. Unassigned: a grey dashed avatar "+" (as the Members cell already uses), not purple "Assign". Due date plain text, red only when late. Hover keeps Edit in the ⋮ (no floating Edit over the date). findings.title: AI brief: made-up “n× more often” figures and advice blind to the lead’s age
findings.now: Every stage has a canned brief: “Call or WhatsApp within 24h: leads contacted same-day reach Met 3.1× more often” on Olivia (50 days in New, tag “FRESH LEAD · RESPOND FAST”); Vivien (55 days in Quote Sent) reads “Quote sent. Check in on day 3 …” with tag “FOLLOW UP · DAY 3”; Gerald (56 days in Met) “Send the quote within 5 days … win 1.8× more often”, tag “QUOTE WINDOW · 5 DAYS”; Muthu (Lost 47 days ago, reason already logged as “No response from lead”) “Log the reason while it is fresh”. Show more stacks two more full cards, each again headed “MAISON AI BRIEF” with its own orange CAPS tag (“BUDGET FIT · STRONG MATCH”, “PREPARE THE FIRST CALL”) and two more outlined buttons — 6 purple buttons. Tags elsewhere: “PARKED · SET A NUDGE”, “LEARN FROM THE LOSS”, “THE PROJECT”.
findings.why: The ratios are not the studio’s numbers (lib/leads/briefs.ts says the copy is invented and scripted per stage), so the card states things the record does not back (Principle 11 · Honest data) and is visibly wrong on most demo leads — a studio owner stops trusting the one card that sits first on every lead. Six purple buttons above the cards are the loudest thing on the page.
findings.proposal: Keep ONE brief card, written from the record: its age and what is missing (“Olivia has been waiting 50 days — no one owns her yet”). Delete every “n× more often” clause unless it is computed from the studio’s own Reports figures. Tag: drop it, or sentence-case grey text, never uppercase orange. One outlined action (the one that matches the header’s next step); the second moves to the FAB sheet. Remove Show more / the stacked briefs. The eyebrow reads “Maison AI” once.

findings.title: The same facts are printed three or four times on one lead page
findings.now: Header: name + four CAPS meta chips “9123 4567 · S$ 70.5K · HDB 4-ROOM · INSTAGRAM”. Info column: the name again in 28px, “9123 4567”, then Lead info “Stage New · Source Instagram · Budget (S$) 70,500” and Property info “Type HDB 4-Room”. AI brief: “New inquiry from Instagram — HDB 4-Room, S$70.5K budget, keys collected.” Stage is shown three times (“Stage: New ▾”, Lead info › Stage “New”, LEAD STAGES “New · current · 50 days”). Budget in three formats: “S$ 70.5K”, “70,500”, “S$70.5K”. The header chips repeat on all 9 tabs.
findings.why: A studio owner reads the same phone, budget, type and source three times before reaching anything new; the page reads as dense even though most of it is repetition. Three budget formats look like three different numbers.
findings.proposal: Drop the four meta chips from the lead header (keep only real status chips such as Return processing) — the info column is the one home of contact and property facts. Remove the “Stage” row from Lead info (the Stage ▾ pill and LEAD STAGES say it). The brief stops restating source/type/budget. One money format on the record: “S$ 70,500” (lib/format moneyCard).

findings.title: A column of “--” placeholders on every lead
findings.now: Olivia’s column: “Owner --”, “NRIC / FIN --”, “Customer ID --”, “Portal --”, “District --”, “Area size (sq ft) --”, “Remarks --” — seven empty rows; every other demo lead shows the same five to seven. LEAD STAGES adds “--” on each future stage (Contacted · Met · Quote Sent · Won) and Next follow-up “None set --” (Mei Ling).
findings.why: Empty rows are reading work with no answer; the identity details a studio actually uses (owner, address, budget) are lost among dashes. NRIC / FIN and Customer ID sit high in Lead info though most leads never have them.
findings.proposal: Show only filled rows. Under each section one text link “Add district, area size…” (or “Add details · 6 empty”) that opens Edit details on the first empty field (the form already opens on a row, REG-224). Move NRIC / FIN and Customer ID into Other info. LEAD STAGES: future stages carry no “--” (an empty circle says “not yet”).

findings.area: Lead › Overview (cards’ empty states) · Meetings tab
findings.title: Two filled buttons on most lead pages (header + an empty card)
findings.now: Header primary is filled (“Move to Quote Sent”, “Resume at Contacted”, “Convert to Project”) and the Overview’s empty cards each carry their own filled button: QUOTES “From Scratch” + filled “From Template”; MY TASKS filled “+ Create New Task” (On Hold); FILES “Create Folder” + filled “Upload Files” (Quote Sent). The quote card’s choice “From Scratch / From Template” is also a decision the Create Quote window already asks.

findings.route: /leads/[id] (New lead with no owner), phone stage sheet
findings.title: The filled button offers a move the page knows it will refuse
findings.now: Olivia (New, no owner): filled “Move to Contacted” → snackbar “Assign a member first · Assign”. Beside it the outlined “🔒 Convert to Project” → the same snackbar. On a phone the LEAD STAGES rows read “Assign a member first” four times (Contacted, Met, Quote Sent, Won); the listing’s phone stage sheet repeats “Complete Contacted first” three times under a filled “Move to Contacted”. Every pre-Won lead carries the locked Convert to Project button (New, Contacted, Met, On Hold, Lost).
findings.why: The page’s loudest control leads to a refusal, and the real next step (assign someone) is a small purple link in the column. A locked button that can’t act is noise (page-checklist ③ “Nothing that can’t act”); the same refusal printed four times is repetition.
findings.proposal: When the lead has no owner, the header’s filled button is “Assign a member” (opens the Assign popover; the move follows once saved, as the phone already chains Assign-then-move). Drop the locked Convert to Project from the header; Won stays reachable in Stage ▾, where its row carries the reason (“Complete Quote Sent first”). Phone LEAD STAGES: one line under the card (“Assign a member to move Olivia on”), not one per stage.

findings.title: Every row repeats purple actions; hover tools cover the row’s own cells
findings.now: Measured 24 purple text/icons in the first screen (39 on the kanban). Rows with no task show purple “+ Add task”; every row has an outlined-purple “assign” icon button after the avatars; Olivia’s row shows “👤+ Assign” as text instead. On hover the row floats an outlined “Edit” and a purple-outlined ⋮ over the Property type / Created cells (“Others” → “Other”, “BTO 4…”). The ⋮ (row and kanban card) holds a single item, “Delete”, for most leads.
findings.why: The listing is the most-used screen; a column of identical purple controls is what the eye lands on instead of names and stages. The hover band hides data. A menu with one destructive item is a click to reach Delete and nothing else.
findings.proposal: Assign icon and “+ Add task” appear on row hover / focus only (grey “No task” at rest); one style for an unowned lead (the same icon, not a text link). Drop the hover “Edit” (a row press opens the lead; Edit lives in the lead’s ⋮ and the row ⋮). The row ⋮ is the grey house IconButton, not primary, and sits in its own last column so nothing is covered. Keep ⋮ only when it holds more than Delete, else Delete moves into the bulk bar.

findings.title: “Qanvast Ops” mixes the studio’s Qanvast account with an operator console
findings.now: Rail item and every page title read “Qanvast Ops”. Tabs: Leads · Studios · Lead credits · Reviews · Hangouts. Studios is OpenMaison’s operator view of the studio itself: “DEMO STUDIO · /my/demo-studio”, head “OPENMAISON’S SWITCHES · ON”, two live switches “Client portal — Open — clients sign in at /my/demo-studio” and “Messages — Sending — the studio’s emails and WhatsApp messages leave as they happen”; Maison AI asks “Which studios’ clients use the portal most?”. Dane (the studio’s Owner) can flip them.
findings.why: “Ops” is an insider word; a studio owner reads this place as “my Qanvast leads, credits and reviews”. The Studios tab is a platform admin page — a studio owner can switch off their own client portal and messages from a page that says it is OpenMaison’s, and “Studios” (plural) means nothing to one studio.
findings.proposal: Rail and title: “Qanvast” (the mock’s word; REG-77 renamed it — ask Vicky). Hide the Studios tab from studio roles (it belongs to an OpenMaison operator role); if a studio needs to see the two states, show them read-only on Company › Client portal as “Paused by OpenMaison”.

findings.title: The same next step is drawn 3–5 times on one project page
findings.now: Ryan’s project: the header’s filled “Review the ask for more time”; the Maison AI brief’s outlined “Review the ask for more time”; the Overview’s Needs you row “More time on Carpentry fabrication · Approve · Decline”; a second Needs you row “Carpentry fabrication · Was due Wed 21 Oct · 6 days late · Mark done”; the Schedule tab’s purple banner “Michelle asks for more time on Carpentry fabrication. Open it”; and the milestone panel’s own “Approve · Decline” band. Marcus (Setting up): “Start the project” in the header (filled), in the brief (outlined) and as “Start the project · Start” in Before work starts. Aisha (On hold): “Resume” in the header, the brief and the Needs you row “On hold since 15 Oct ’26 · Resume · Change”.
findings.why: A studio owner reads the same instruction three times and can’t tell whether they are three different jobs. The page looks busier than the work is, and the eye has no single place to start.
findings.proposal: One door per step. Keep the header’s filled button (the page’s one primary) and the Needs you row. The brief stops repeating it: `pair(f.top, …)` in lib/projects/briefs.ts drops `f.top` whenever it equals the header’s label, so the brief offers only the other help (“Draft an update about this week”) — or no buttons at all; the brief is a sentence. Remove the Schedule tab’s ask banner (the row already shows “More time asked” and the panel carries Approve · Decline). Merge the two Carpentry rows into one (“Carpentry is 6 days late — Michelle asks for Wed 28 Oct · Approve”).

findings.area: Projects › Money tab (and the portal’s Money)
findings.title: “Money” names a tab that mixes client payments, supplier costs and profit
findings.now: Tab “Money” → page title “Money”, then “Needs you 4”, tiles “TO COLLECT · TO PAY · PROFIT”, then four regions “Billing” (All · Invoices · Payments · Credit notes), “Changes to the contract” (a table whose head says “VARIATION ORDER”, link “Deleted variation orders”), “Where costs go”, “Costs” (All · Purchase orders · Bills · Expenses). The phone adds a “Billing · Costs” switch above the four billing chips. The client’s portal tab is also “Money”. Company › Finance calls the same two halves “Money in” and “Money out”.

findings.proposal: Rename the tab “Payments” (the owner’s word) and the page title with it; inside, two regions named as studios say them: “Client payments” (was Billing — the stages, invoices, receipts, credit notes) and “Costs” (purchase orders, bills, expenses). “Changes to the contract” → “Variation orders” (the head and the link already say it). Keep Profit as the one tile Owners see. Portal tab “Money” → “Payments”. Finance’s “Money in / Money out” → “Client payments / Costs” so one record has one name in every module.

findings.area: Projects › Overview · Money · invoice papers · Dashboard · Finance
findings.title: One figure — what the client still owes — has six names
findings.now: For Ryan, S$14,018.04 is “To collect” on the Money tile (project-money.tsx:258) and in Finance › To do, “Outstanding” on the Overview’s Money card (money-card.tsx:50), “Owed to you” on the Dashboard’s Pulse, “Balance due” on the invoice paper, “Still owed” on the receipt, and “To pay” in the invoice panel’s totals (invoice-panel.tsx:88). What the studio owes suppliers is “To pay” (Money tile) and “You owe” (Dashboard). Collected is “Collected” (studio) and “Paid so far” (portal). The Overview’s caption “22% · work 29%” and the Money tile’s “Cash so far S$4,750.86” add two more unexplained figures.
findings.why: An owner comparing the Dashboard with a project cannot tell these are the same number; “To pay” means “the client still has to pay” in one panel and “we still have to pay” on the tile next to it.
findings.proposal: One studio word each, everywhere: “To collect” (client → studio) and “To pay” (studio → suppliers); “Collected” for money in. Overview card: “Outstanding” → “To collect”. Dashboard Pulse: “Owed to you” → “To collect”, “You owe” → “To pay”. Invoice panel totals: “To pay” → “To collect”. Client papers keep the client’s words (“Balance due”, “Paid so far”) — and the receipt’s “Still owed” → “Balance due” to match the invoice. “work 29%” → “29% of the work done”; “Cash so far” → “Cash in hand (collected − paid out)” with the sum in the tooltip.

findings.title: “Stage” means three different things on one project
findings.now: The header’s “Stage: In progress ▾” (the project’s lifecycle: Setting up · In progress · Completed); the Money tab’s “STAGE” column and the Overview’s “Payment stages · 4” (Deposit · Commencement · Mid-Project · Completion); and the client’s portal calls the milestones “stages”: “2 of 7 stages done”, “Electrical is paused”, “the stages ahead and when each is planned”, while the studio’s Schedule says “2 of 7 milestones”.
findings.why: A studio owner telling a client “we’re at the Mid-Project stage” and the client reading “stage 3 of 7” are talking about different things. Three meanings of one word on one record invites wrong answers on the phone.
findings.proposal: Keep “Stage” for the project’s lifecycle only (Setting up · In progress · Completed). Payment parts become “Payments” (“Payment stages · 4” → “Payments · 4”; the Billing column head “Stage” → “Payment”). The portal says what the studio says: “2 of 7 milestones done” — or, if milestones reads too technical for homeowners, use “steps” on BOTH sides (studio Schedule “2 of 7 steps”). One word per thing.

findings.title: Money tab: four filled buttons, up to three verbs a row, “Open” beside every ⋮
findings.now: At 1440 the first screen has four filled buttons: the header’s “Review the ask for more time”, and “Pay”, “Confirm”, “Change it” on the Needs you banners. The banner rows carry “Open · Pay”, “See the bank’s confirmation · Not received · Confirm”, “Open · Change it”. In Billing, Changes to the contract and Costs every row ends with a purple “Open” (or “Record a payment”, “Pay back”, “Change it”, “Pay”) AND a ⋮, though the row’s name already opens the same panel. On a phone each billing card carries a “Next step · Open ⋮” line.
findings.why: Thirty-odd purple words and four filled buttons on one screen: nothing stands out, so nothing gets done first. “Open” next to a name that opens is pure repetition.
findings.proposal: House rule for rows: ONE verb, the rest in ⋮ (PortalMenu + DropdownItem). Needs you banners: the verb as the DS outlined button, not filled (needs-list.tsx:209) — “See the bank’s confirmation” and “Not received” move into the row’s ⋮; “Open” goes (the title opens it). Tables: drop the “Open” fallback in `inv.nextStep` (billing-section.tsx:96) — a row shows a verb only when a real next step exists (Record a payment, Pay, Pay back). The phone card loses the “Next step ·” label (the verb sits in the card foot beside ⋮). The page keeps one filled button: the header’s.

findings.title: Overview text is squeezed into narrow columns at 1440

findings.title: The same money is named 4–5 ways across Finance, project Money and Reports
findings.now: What clients still owe: "To collect" (Finance › To do section; project Money tile), "Owed" (Money in column; To do caption "S$57,825.65 owed on 4 invoices"), "Owed to you" (Reports › Finance tab and tile), "Still owed" (report invoice column), "Outstanding" (code) and "Balance" (Client statement). What the studio owes: "To pay" (To do; project Money tile), "You owe" (Reports tab), "Owed" (Vendors column), "Still owed" (Vendor spend report), "still to pay" (Money out caption). "Payments" means client payments (Money in › Payments, project Billing chip), commission paid (Commission › "Payments"), and the paid-out list is "Paid" (chip) / "Payments out" (its own title). "Money in" is the Finance tab with invoices, VOs and credit notes, but in Cash flow "MONEY IN" = "Client payments, 2026". The project calls its invoices "Billing"; Reports call them "Revenue".
findings.why: A studio owner reconciling "Owed to you S$34,802.98" (Reports) against "To collect S$57,825.65" (To do) cannot tell whether they are the same thing (they are not — one is sent invoices, the other includes drafts ready to send). One word per idea is the only way the figures can be trusted.
findings.proposal: Glossary, applied everywhere: client money still due = "To collect" (Reports tab "Owed to you" → "To collect"; Money in column "Owed" → "To collect"; "Still owed" → "To collect"); studio money still due = "To pay" (Reports tab "You owe" → "To pay"; Vendors column "Owed" → "To pay"; Vendor spend "Still owed" → "To pay"); a client's money received = "Client payments" (Money in kind "Payments" → "Client payments"); money paid out = "Payments out" (Money out kind "Paid" → "Payments out", matching its title); commission paid = "Commission paid" (Commission › "Payments"); the project Money list "Billing" → "Invoices"; Reports keep "Revenue" only inside Profit and loss, with Cash flow's tile "Money in" → "Received". Where a figure differs on purpose (sent invoices vs sent + ready drafts), say so in the caption: "S$34,802.98 to collect on sent invoices".

findings.title: Two different "Profit" figures and two margins on two tabs of the same report
findings.now: Profit and loss (This year): "PROFIT S$71,264.01 · Revenue less costs" and "MARGIN ON WHAT WAS INVOICED 64.5% · Healthy · before GST". Profitability: "PROFIT S$88,161.92 · Contract value less committed costs, on 2 projects with costs past a tenth of the contract" and "MARGIN ON CONTRACTS 70.9% · Weighted by contract value · early estimates left out"; its table help: "Profit = contract value − committed costs, both with GST (the Money tab’s figure) — “--” until its costs pass a tenth of the contract." (REG: the two margins are named apart on purpose — lib/finance/reports.ts:10.)
findings.why: An owner sees two profits a click apart, one before GST and one with GST, one on invoices and one on contracts, and concludes the numbers are wrong. Naming them apart does not survive a glance at two big numbers both labelled "Profit".

findings.title: The same kind of decision has different verbs: Approve / Agree / Answer / Publish / Review

findings.why: Wrong label on the record's link, a doubled date and a third name for vendors erode trust in small ways on the most-used panel.
findings.proposal: Label "Project" (or "For") when the task is on a project. The field shows "Tue, 27 Oct ’26 · 10:00 AM" once, no helper. "Add a vendor or contractor". Sentence case: "Mark as done", "Attach files", "Add tag". While a Drawer is open its footer holds the one filled button (already); the header button is behind the scrim — fine.

findings.title: Six date styles and two "ago" styles in one lane
findings.now: "Tuesday 27 October" (greeting) · "Tue, 27 Oct ’26 · 10:00 AM" (Tasks) · "27/10/2026, 10:00 AM" (task field) · "Due Wed, 28 Oct ’26" (bell) · "18 Oct" (Needs you) · "Reported 18 Oct ’26" (tickets) · "Starts 5 Nov" vs "Resumes 29 Nov ’26" (Projects card, one card) · "yesterday", "2 days ago" (Dashboard) vs "1d ago", "7d ago", "14d ago" (bell, Messages, Tickets).
findings.why: Inconsistent dates make a list hard to scan and look unfinished.
findings.proposal: One rule (lib/format): this year "Tue 27 Oct" (no year, no comma), other years "27 Oct 2025"; with a time "Tue 27 Oct, 10:00 am"; relative times spelled "7 days ago" / "yesterday" everywhere (no "7d"); the date field shows the same words.

findings.title: Counts are written five ways: "Needs you 51", "Overdue · 6", "All Tasks (48)", "Open (3)", "4 to approve"
findings.now: Dashboard head grey number after the title "Needs you 51" and tabs "To approve 8"; Tasks chips with a middle dot "Overdue · 6" and pill "All Tasks (48)" in parentheses; Tickets chips "Open (3)"; Company panel pills "1 awaiting"; bell eyebrow "DUE 14" with the number at the far right; Messages chips carry no counts (by design).
findings.why: A count format that changes per page is visual noise and makes the house look stitched together.
findings.proposal: One count style: the label then a grey number, no punctuation — "Overdue 6", "All tasks 48", "Open 3", "Approvals 4" (the Dashboard tabs' style). Use it in the house Chips, ScopePill and Tabs so every page inherits it.

findings.title: Four different looks for "filter this list": text tabs, segmented, outlined chips, bordered chips
findings.now: Dashboard Needs you: borderless text tabs with a tinted selected one; Dashboard Studio/Mine: grey-track SegmentedButton; Tasks: segmented "All · Leads · Projects" + outlined purple to-do chips with icons; Tickets: small bordered chips with bold 13px labels "Open (3)"; Messages: bordered chips "All · Unread · Clients · Team".
findings.why: The same job (narrow a list) is drawn four ways in one lane; the user can't learn one pattern.
findings.proposal: In-list filters are the house `Chips` everywhere (Tickets, Messages, Tasks to-do chips, Dashboard tabs) with one size; `SegmentedButton` only for view switches (Studio/Mine, table/board). Remove Tasks' Leads/Projects segment (1-06).

findings.title: On a phone the to-do chips lose their words: just "⏱ 6", "📅 6", "👤+ 15"
findings.now: At 390 the chips are icon + number only (no labels, no tooltip on touch); the approvals banner takes the top 100px; 48 tasks render as tall cards (page height 10,104px).
findings.why: A clock and a number don't say "overdue" to someone who hasn't learned the icon.
findings.proposal: Keep the words in a ChipRail on the phone ("Overdue 6 · Today 6 · Unassigned 15"); drop the banner (1-06); open the phone list on My tasks with Overdue + Today first.

findings.title: On a phone every card and row has its own ⋮ and verb line; Studio/Mine takes a row
findings.now: Under the greeting a full row holds only "Studio | Mine" and the page ⋮; Needs you has a card ⋮ and every row a ⋮ plus a verb on a third line ("Publish ⋮", "Review ⋮"); 11 ⋮ in the first two screens; the floating "Ask Maison AI…" pill sits over the fourth row's verb at rest; Pulse moves below Needs you.
findings.why: Three-line rows and a ⋮ everywhere double the scroll on the phone, where the Dashboard is opened most.
findings.proposal: Phone: Studio/Mine moves into the page ⋮ (one ⋮ for the page). Row = title + caption, the verb at the row's right as on the desk; the row's other actions on long-press / its pane. Card ⋮ removed (hide cards from the page ⋮). Pad the list's end so the dock pill never covers a verb.

findings.title: Every card on Your profile opens with a two-line explanation
findings.now: "Your name and photo show wherever you appear in the studio — on the leads you hold, the quotes you prepare and in the messages clients read." · "It prints on the quotes and contracts you prepare, once you allow it. Draw it, type your name in the signature face, or upload a picture of it." · "Where the studio pays you — a claim paid back, your commission. Finance shows it, with a copy button, when it pays you." · "What reaches you, and how. Which notices go out at all is the studio’s choice, in Settings › Notifications." · "What clients read about you — your card and your work — on their portal and your studio’s Hangout pages." · "Whether you take new leads and the leads you prefer are on your row in Company › Members." Plus field helpers "Printed as your email on the quotes you prepare", "A mobile signs you in and gets WhatsApp notices; clients see it on their portal", "You’re an Owner at Demo Studio. An Owner or an Admin sets roles on Company › Members.", "Off, the studio signature box stays blank and you sign by hand. You can change this any time."
findings.why: Nine explanatory sentences on a page that holds name, phone, signature, PayNow and notifications. The page reads like a manual.
findings.proposal: Keep one short helper only where it changes a decision: under the signature switch "Off: you sign printed quotes by hand". Card titles carry the rest: "Your details", "Signature", "PayNow — for claims and commission", "Notifications", "Public profile", "New leads". Drop the role sentence (show "Owner" as a chip by the name). "Hangout pages" → "your studio’s public pages".

findings.title: L1 headers carry different kits: create + Insights + ⋮, create only, nothing, or create in the toolbar
findings.now: Leads: "Add Lead" filled + "Insights" outlined + ⋮. Projects: "New project" + "Insights" + ⋮, then a stat strip of four grey boxes and a fifth bare "CONTRACT VALUE S$ 261.9K" tile. Tools › Quotes: no header action; a second title "All Quotes" + "Waiting on client · 3" + outlined "Create Quote" + ⋮ in the toolbar. Tasks: "Add Task" + ⋮. Tickets: "New ticket" only. "Insights" opens Company › Reports (two names for one place).
findings.why: Where the create button and the page menu sit should never need hunting.
findings.proposal: Header anatomy for every L1: title · (one filled "New …") · ⋮; reports reached from the ⋮ or the rail ("Reports", not "Insights"). Tools › Quotes drops the second "All Quotes" title. The Projects stat strip uses one StatTile look for all five.

findings.title: One contact log, two vocabularies (desk form vs phone sheet)
findings.now: Desk (Notes › New › Contact Log): “Contacted via* WhatsApp · Email · SMS · Call · In person · Others”, “Date & Time*”, “Outcome*” as a select, “Attach screenshots of your call attempts”, “Save”. Phone log sheet: “How did the call with Farah go?”, “How: Call · WhatsApp · Site visit · Note · More…”, “When: Now · 4:46 PM · Change”, “How it went: Connected · Callback requested · Meeting scheduled · No response · Not interested” as chips, “Save log”. The Move stage window’s read-only Contacted log adds “Preferred mode”, “Schedule a call/meeting (optional) — If you wish to be reminded, a task will be created.”
findings.why: The same record is asked for in two orders with two names for the channel (“In person” vs “Site visit”) and the outcome; a member who logs on both devices meets two forms. The phone’s wording is plainer.
findings.proposal: One vocabulary, the phone’s: “How” (Call · WhatsApp · Visit · Email · SMS · Other), “When”, “How it went” as chips at every width, button “Save log”. Rename “Preferred mode” → “Call back by”; helper → “We’ll add a task to remind you.”

findings.title: Prototype and demo talk printed to studios
findings.now: Every Qanvast account page ends with “Simulated on this prototype — the credits follow your Qanvast leads and returns here, the reviews follow your finished projects and published work; the contract, rank, page views and Singapore’s averages are samples, and a reply is kept here, not posted to Qanvast.” Hangouts: “Sample Hangouts written for the demo — Qanvast’s own events come through its feed.” + “Sample” on every card + a “SAMPLE” chip on the event header. Planned meeting: “Listening isn’t connected in this prototype — type what’s said, or paste a transcript.” Qanvast leads: four sort heads and “Request Leads” answer “Coming soon”.
findings.why: Studios in a live demo read “prototype”, “samples” and “not posted” as “this doesn’t work”. A 40-word disclaimer under every page is the longest paragraph on it.
findings.proposal: Remove these lines from the pages; if the demo must say it, one shell-level “Demo data” chip in the page header (one place, one word). Sort heads that don’t sort lose their arrows; Request Leads hides until it works (or opens the Qanvast account manager’s WhatsApp).

findings.area: Qanvast Ops › Lead credits · Reviews · Hangout page
findings.title: Sub-views are chips on two tabs, Tabs on the next; Reviews has two chip rows
findings.now: Lead credits: chips “Overview · Transactions · Contracts”. Reviews: chips “Reviews · Ranking · Feedback”, then a second chip row “All · Waiting for a reply · 2 · Replied” plus “All ratings ▾” and “Newest first ▾”. A Hangout page uses the house Tabs “Plan · Chats 3 · How it went” for the same job, then chips “All · 3 / Waiting · 3 / On now · 0 / Done · 0”. Projects puts views as Chips in the body’s title line.
findings.why: The same kind of switch (which view of this section) looks like a filter on one page and like a tab on the next; two stacked chip rows are the Marketplace noise the owner called out.
findings.proposal: One rule: a section’s views are second-level house Tabs (the hangout page’s), chips are only filters. Reviews then keeps one chip row (All · Waiting for a reply · Replied) and folds the rating and sort into one “Sort” menu.

findings.area: Counts across Leads, Meetings, Qanvast Ops
findings.title: Five count formats for “how many” in one module
findings.now: Parentheses: “All Leads (31)”, “Review imported leads (14)”, “Google Ads (2)”, “Approve All Clean (13)”, “Briefs to save (3)”, “Notes to write up (2)”, “Show only duplicates (1)”. Middle dot: “All · 3”, “Waiting for a reply · 2”, “FILES · 13”, “Upcoming · 3”, “Overdue · 1”. Bare: kanban “New 7”, scope menu “Mine 14”. Red badge: tabs “Tasks 3”, “Questionnaire 4”, hangout “Chats 3”. Plus “+2” chips in task cells.
findings.why: Each format suggests a different kind of number (a total, a filter, an alert); the red badge reads as “something is wrong” for routine open tasks.
findings.proposal: Chips, pills and card heads: “Label · n” (house middle dot) everywhere — the scope pill “All leads · 31”. Red badge only for things overdue or waiting on you; open-task counts on tabs in the neutral count style.

findings.title: Title Case and sentence case mixed in buttons, menus and column names
findings.now: Title Case: “Add Lead”, “Create New Lead”, “Import from File”, “Lead Import History”, “Deleted Leads”, “Leads Settings”, “Copy Link”, “Invite to Portal”, “Return Lead”, “Ask Client”, “View Client Info”, “Assign Member”, “Add Task”, “Create New Task”, “Use Template”, “Save all as Template”, “Manage Templates”, “Create Quote”, “New Contract”, “New File”, “From Local Files”, “Clear All”, “Approve All Clean”, “View & Merge”, “Reject New”, “Keep Both”, “Merge into Existing”, “Empty Trash”, “Delete Forever”, “Save & Move”, “Download Skipped Records”, “Auto Fill”, “Add Log”, “Contact Log”. Sentence case beside them: “Add task”, “Plan a meeting”, “Start a meeting now”, “From the studio agreement”, “Export all as…”, “Request reviews”, “Ask homeowners for a review”. Column names: “Lead Name”, “Property Type” next to “In stage”, “Last contact”, “Next follow-up”.
findings.why: Reads unfinished, and the same control appears in two spellings (“Add task” / “Add Task”, “Contact log” / “Contact Log”).
findings.proposal: Sentence case for every button, menu row, tab-toolbar action, chip and column name (“Add lead”, “Create new lead”, “Lead name”, “Property type”, “Contact log”…); proper nouns keep capitals (Qanvast, WhatsApp, Maison AI).

findings.area: Create verbs on the lead’s tabs
findings.title: Every tab names “create” differently
findings.now: Tasks: toolbar “Add Task ▾” (rows “Create New Task” · “Use Template”) and a table foot “+ Add Task”; listing cell “+ Add task”; empty state “Create New Task”; phone quick add “Add a task…”. Quotes: “Create Quote” (no menu). Contracts: “New Contract ▾”. Files: folder icon + “New File ▾” (“From Local Files · From Google Drive”). Notes: “New ▾” (“Note · Contact Log”). Meetings: “New Meeting ▾” and empty “Plan a meeting”. Leads: header “Add Lead ▾” opens a dialog titled “Create New Lead” whose button is “Create”.
findings.why: A studio member looks for a different word on every tab; “Add / Create / New” for the same act makes the toolbars feel unrelated.
findings.proposal: One verb, “New”: “New task ▾”, “New quote”, “New contract ▾”, “New file ▾”, “New note ▾”, “New meeting ▾”, header “New lead ▾”; the dialog title “New lead”, its button “Add lead”. Drop the Tasks table’s second “+ Add Task” foot row on desk (the toolbar holds it).

findings.title: Owner and Members show the same person twice, under a third heading
findings.now: Section “Collaborators”: “Owner You” then “Members D Dane” (Dane is you) — the same person named two ways; Vivien: “Owner Sarah / Members S Sarah”; Olivia: “Owner --” and a link “Assign Member ›”. The listing column, Settings and REG-290 say “Members”; the Assign popover is titled “Assign Member” though it ticks several; Hangout report says “By designer · Designer”; Meetings column says “People”. Same in the project’s info column.
findings.why: Three names (Collaborators / Members / People / Designer) for the studio people on a record; “You” and “Dane” read as two people.
findings.proposal: Section title “Members”. One list: “Dane (you) · Owner” on the first row, the others below; no separate Owner row. Link “Assign members”, popover “Assign members”. Meetings column “Members”; Hangout table “Member”.

findings.title: “New” is a stage, a not-opened mark and a property condition
findings.now: Phone card: a blue “NEW” tag beside the name AND the stage pill “New” under it. Scope menu: “Unseen 2”. Rail/dock badge counts unseen as “2 new”. Dashboard: “new lead, no contact yet”. Property info: “Condition New”. Desk: the not-opened mark is the left purple band with no word.
findings.why: On a phone the user sees “NEW” twice and can’t tell the stage from “not opened yet”; “Unseen” is software talk.
findings.proposal: Not-opened = “Not opened” (phone tag removed — the band carries it, as on the desk), scope row “Not opened yet”; stage stays “New”; condition value “New (never lived in)” or “BTO / new launch”.

findings.title: Import review: a permanent banner, green buttons and the same tag on every card
findings.now: A docked bar “Review imported leads (14) · 1 DUPLICATE” sits at the foot of the listing on every visit (14 rows waiting since 9 Sep). Inside: off-palette green filled “Approve All Clean (13)”, red “Reject” + green “Approve” text on every card, a “PENDING” tag on 13 of 14 cards, source chips “Google Ads (2) · Instagram (2) …”, dates “22d ago” on one card and “9 Sep ’26” on the rest, detail rows “—”, two address fields “Address” and “Lead address”.
findings.why: A bar that never leaves trains people to ignore it; repeated coloured verbs on every card and a tag that every card shares carry no information; green filled is not the house primary.
findings.proposal: Move the queue into the scope pill’s TO DO group (“To review · 14”) and drop the docked bar; the Leads rail badge can include it. In the sheet: no tag when the state is the default (only “Duplicate” shows), no verbs on the cards — Reject / Approve live once in the detail pane foot; the bulk button is the house primary “Approve 13 (no duplicates)”. One date format; one address field.

findings.title: Key facts truncated; Response time reads like the lead is Won
findings.now: Rows cut with “…”: “Next follow-up Call home …”, “Response time Assigned — 50 days running · First c…”, “Last contact WhatsApp · Meeting schedul…”. Olivia’s full Response time is “Assigned — 50 days running · First contact in 28h · Won — 49 days running” on a New lead; others read “Assigned in 2h · First contact in 24.8h”.
findings.why: The house rule says a read-in-full surface never truncates (page-checklist, REG-212). “Won — 49 days running” on a New lead is misread as a Won lead; “24.8h” is a stopwatch, not a studio word.
findings.proposal: Let these rows wrap to two lines. Response time in words: “Not assigned for 50 days · first reply in about a day”; drop the Won leg until the lead reaches Quote Sent; round hours (“about a day”, “2 hours”).

findings.title: Questionnaire: “Q:/A:” prefixes, a purple “Answer” per row, raw answers
findings.now: Every row “Q: Do you have pets? … Answer” (purple, ×4), answered rows “Q: … By Studio” tag + grey band “A: 81234567 · 10 Sep ’26 ✎”, “A: 28/11/2026”, “A: Yes”. Summary card “QUESTIONNAIRE SUMMARY · Total questions answered 7 / 11 · Client answered: 0 · Studio answered: 7” — the Overview card repeats it word for word. Toolbar “Ask Client”.
findings.why: Prefixes and per-row purple links add reading without meaning; the phone answer isn’t grouped (the house phone format is “8123 4567”) and the date isn’t the house date.
findings.proposal: Question as the row title, the answer under it in body text (no Q:/A:). Unanswered rows: grey “Not answered” + the row opens the answer box (no repeated purple link). Tag “By studio” → small grey “Answered by the studio”. Format answers by type (phone, date). Summary: one line “7 of 11 answered · none by Olivia yet”. Button “Ask Olivia”.

findings.title: Task titles cut short while tags and statuses shout in capitals
findings.now: Titles ellipsised at ~25 characters (“Book the showroom visit…”, “Send the revised …”) in a table with room to spare; Tags “GENERIC · FOCUS · +2” in capitals on three rows; Status “COMPLETED” beside a green tick that already says done, “OPEN” on the rest; every due date underlined like a link; purple “Assign” and “+ Add Tags” per row; a calendar icon button for “no due date”; two adds (“Add Task ▾” and “+ Add Task”). Measured 17 purple, 24 uppercase, 5 truncated.
findings.why: The task’s name is the one thing to read; the row gives it the least room. Tags are the studio’s own words and shouldn’t be capitalised for them.
findings.proposal: Title column takes the spare width by default (the column settings model allows it); tags in the case typed; Status column off by default (the tick says it) or plain grey words; due dates not underlined; Assign / Add tags appear on hover; drop the foot “+ Add Task” on desk.

findings.title: Meeting statuses and scores in insider words
findings.now: Status column: “To write up — Its planned time has passed” (cut), “Held — Brief to save”, “Upcoming”. Meeting column: “Meeting — Logged at Met”, “First consultation — Written up from notes”. Column “Deal score”: “57 · Cool”, “53 · Cool”, “--” on 9 of 12 rows; “People” column “--” on 7 rows. Toolbar: outlined chips “Briefs to save (3)” and “Notes to write up (2)”, filled “New Meeting ▾”, “Insights”. Phone: the chips shrink to bare “📄 3” and “≡ 2”, and the card ⋮ is purple.
findings.why: “Brief”, “write up”, “logged at Met”, “Cool” are the tool’s own words; a studio owner wants “which meetings still need notes”. A column that is mostly “--” is noise.
findings.proposal: Status words: “Upcoming”, “Needs notes” (time passed, nothing written), “Held”, “Summary not saved”. Meeting caption: “From the Met step” / “From notes”. Deal score off by default (keep in Column settings), shown as “Likely · 57” with Hot/Warm/Cool renamed “Likely / Maybe / Unlikely”. Chips “Summaries to save · 3” / “Needs notes · 2”; on a phone keep the words. ⋮ grey.

findings.title: A held meeting is ten cards and says the concerns three times
findings.now: Cards: SUMMARY · NEXT STEPS · MESSAGE TO SEND · WHAT WE HEARD · CONCERNS THEY RAISED · 3 · THE NOTES | ON THE LEAD · DEAL SCORE · ROUGH ESTIMATE · THE MEETING. Concerns: “Concerns Timeline, Price, Competition” row + tags (“Budget concern · Likes modern · Landed owner · Timeline urgent · Comparing IDs · Wants kitchen · Wants bedroom · Wants bathroom · Premium client”) + the Concerns card. Summary foot “Made from the notes, by rule.” Answers headed “Demo Studio Pte Ltd’s answer · “6–10 weeks is too long””. Header filled “Save to the lead” and the ON THE LEAD card’s own “Save”. The FAB covers the add-ons’ prices (“+S$ 2,80…”). Header chips “HELD · WED, 26 AUG ’26 · 12:00 PM · IN PERSON” in capitals.
findings.why: After a meeting the studio wants: what they want, what to do next, the message to send. Everything else competes; “by rule” and “Pte Ltd’s answer” are system words.
findings.proposal: Left column: Summary · Next steps · Message to send; “What we heard” folds its tags under a “Show details”; Concerns card keeps the answers, the duplicate row goes. Cut “Made from the notes, by rule.” → nothing (or “From your notes”). “Our answer”. Drop the card’s Save (the header’s is the one). Header chips sentence case.

findings.title: Red alert badges for routine counts
findings.now: Lead tabs “Tasks 3”, “Questionnaire 4” in red filled badges (open tasks, unanswered questions); the project strip has five red badges (Tasks 2 · Schedule 1 · Client 3 · Design 1 · Money 6); the rail shows six red badges at once (Tasks 1, Projects 3, Leads 2, Company 6, Messages 1, Notifications 16).
findings.why: When everything is red nothing is urgent; a studio owner can’t tell an overdue payment from three normal open tasks.
findings.proposal: Tab counts in the neutral count style (grey) and red only when something is overdue; the rail keeps red for Notifications and Messages only, the rest as a small neutral dot or number (REG-1182 set the count rule — ask Vicky about the colour).

findings.title: Empty-state sentences that are ungrammatical, vague or dead ends
findings.now: Quotes: “Create your first quote · Create quotes and share it with your clients” (also Contracts: “Create contracts and share it with your clients”). Files: “Add your first files · Create folders and upload files from your local.” Tasks: “Add your first task · Stay organised — track, prioritise, and complete everything from one place.” Questionnaire: “No questions yet · Questions are set up by your studio’s admins and will appear here.” (no link to where). Meetings: “Meet with the co-pilot beside you · Plan the meeting, and in it the co-pilot keeps the checklist, the tips and the rough estimate — then makes the brief: what they want, the next steps and the message to send.”
findings.why: “share it” / “from your local” read as typos; marketing lines (“Stay organised…”) tell nothing; the questionnaire one leaves the user stuck; the Meetings paragraph is three lines of feature list.
findings.proposal: Quotes: “No quote yet — make one from a template or upload your own.” Contracts: “No contract yet.” Files: “No files yet — upload photos, plans or documents.” Tasks: “No tasks yet.” Questionnaire: “No questions yet — set them up in Company › Questionnaire” (a link, for Owners/Admins). Meetings: “Plan a meeting and Maison AI keeps notes for you.”

findings.title: At least eight date / time formats in one module
findings.now: “10 Sep ’26, 4:30PM” (Lead returned card — no space), “Thu, 10 Sep ’26 · 6:00 PM” (tasks), “Monday, 7 Sep ’26” (Files day group), “6 Oct ’26・4:42 PM” (Notes list, a different dot), “4/9/2026, 1:45 PM” (Move stage read-only log), “A: 28/11/2026” (Questionnaire), “22d ago” / “2d ago” / “Updated 11 Sep ’26” (review sheet, phone card, kanban), “TUE 27 OCT” / “FRI 20 – SAT 21 NOV” uppercase (Hangouts), “Thu, 29 Oct ’26 at 3:00 PM” vs “THU, 29 OCT ’26 · 3:00 PM” on one meeting page.
findings.why: “4/9/2026” is 4 September in Singapore but 9 April to anyone used to US dates; mixed formats make the same day look different.
findings.proposal: Everything through lib/format: date “Thu, 10 Sep ’26”, time “· 4:30 PM”, relative only for the last 7 days (“2 days ago”, never “2d”); no all-caps dates; the read-only log uses the DateTimeField’s display.

findings.title: Quote card prints six status words and “Private / Shared” on every lead
findings.now: Under the total: “OM-10001 · Private” and a six-step track labelled “Draft · Sent for Approval · Approved · Sent to Client · Confirmed · Signed” plus a CAPS chip “DRAFT” / “APPROVED” / “SIGNED”. Vivien’s lead is in Quote Sent while its quote reads “APPROVED” (not sent to the client).
findings.why: Six labels to say one state; “Private” is unclear (private from whom?). A Quote Sent lead whose quote was never sent is a contradiction the card should surface.
findings.proposal: Show the status once as a plain line: “Approved — not sent to Vivien yet” with the track unlabelled (or only the current step’s word). “Private” → “Only your studio can see it”, “Shared” → “Vivien can see it”.

findings.title: Hangouts: a filled button on every card and a CAPS line on every chat
findings.now: List: filled “Open today’s chats” and filled “Apply” on two cards, outlined “See how it went” on the third, “Sample” on each, uppercase “TUE 27 OCT · HOURS · VENUE · YOUR COST”. Chats tab: three filled “Start” buttons, “BOOKED ON YOUR PAGE” uppercase above every card, a “WAITING” tag on every card while the chip above already filters “Waiting · 3”, “Fits you 80%”.
findings.why: Three filled buttons on one screen; the repeated caps line and tag add nothing the filter doesn’t say.
findings.proposal: One filled button per screen: the next chat’s “Start” is filled, the rest outlined; drop “BOOKED ON YOUR PAGE” (show only the exception, “Walk-in”); no status tag when the filter shows it; “Fits you 80%” → “Good match”. Date eyebrows in sentence case.

findings.title: Qanvast leads table repeats the same value down every row
findings.now: “Return window: Expired (30 days)” on all 7 rows, “Credits 200” on all 7; status tags in capitals (“CONTACTED”, “RETURN PROCESSING”, “RETURN APPROVED · REFUND PROCESSING”); the head “CREAT…” is cut; the page repeats the Leads header (filled “Add Lead”, “Insights”, ⋮ with one row “Export all as…”) plus “Request Leads”.
findings.why: A column with one value is not information; a second copy of the Leads header makes two places to add a lead.
findings.proposal: Return window shows only while open (“12 days left”), blank once expired (the Status says the rest); Credits only when it differs from the usual (or as a total in the pill). Remove Add Lead / Insights from this tab (they belong to Leads). Status chips in the house MetaChip case.

findings.title: “MY TASKS” lists everyone’s tasks on the lead
findings.now: The card is titled “MY TASKS · Tue, 27 Oct” and counts “Upcoming · 3” on Olivia, whose open tasks are unassigned or James’s — not Dane’s. The tab badge says Tasks 3 too.
findings.why: The title promises the viewer’s own work; a member trusts it to be empty when nothing is theirs.
findings.proposal: Title “Open tasks”. If “mine” matters, a second line “1 is yours”. Drop the date from the head (it is today’s date, not the tasks’).

findings.title: Eleven ways to say “create” on one project — Title Case, sentence case, filled, outlined
findings.now: “Add Task ▾” · “Add milestone” · “Post an update” · “New ticket” (FILLED — the only filled create) · “New Meeting ▾” · “Ask Client” · “Add a choice” · “Add a plan” · “New File ▾” (+ a folder icon) · “New ▾” (Notes) · “New ▾” (Money). The phone ⋮’s Create group says “Task · Note · Contact Log · Meeting · Update · Variation order”.
findings.why: Same job, same place, eleven words and two weights: the owner has to read each one; “New ticket” filled competes with the header’s primary.
findings.proposal: One grammar, sentence case, the DS outlined button in the same slot: “New task ▾ · New milestone · New update · New ticket · New meeting ▾ · Ask the client · New choice · New plan · New file ▾ · New note ▾ · New ▾ (Payments)”. “New ticket” becomes outlined (project-tickets.tsx:91). The lead tabs share these toolbars, so the change lands on Leads too.

findings.title: The “Client” tab holds the team’s private chat; “Client” is written three times
findings.now: Tab “Client” → view “Messages” → chips “Client · Team”; each of Ryan’s messages carries a grey “CLIENT” tag; the info column also has “Team chat: Only the team reads it · Messages”. The phone puts “All conversations” beside the views.
findings.why: A private team conversation filed under “Client” is one slip from being sent to the client. The tag on every message tells the owner what the tab already said.
findings.proposal: Messages under Client shows the client conversation only (drop the Client · Team chips). The team’s conversation opens from the info column’s “Team chat” link (already there) and from /chat. Remove the per-message “CLIENT” tag in a client-only thread (keep it only in /chat, where threads mix).

findings.title: A running project’s meetings speak sales: “Logged at Met”, “Deal score”
findings.now: Columns MEETING · WHEN · WHERE · PEOPLE · STATUS · DEAL SCORE; the one row “Meeting / Logged at Met” · “Thu, 30 Jul ’26 · 12:00 PM” · “In person” · “--” · “Held” · “--”.
findings.why: “Met” is a lead stage and “Deal score” a sales measure — neither means anything once the contract is signed; two “--” cells add nothing.
findings.proposal: On a project: hide Deal score (and People when empty) by default; the row’s name says what it was — “First meeting with Ryan” — caption “From the lead, before the project began”.

findings.title: Workload views: insider sentences, nine tiles, a verb on every row
findings.now: Members: “Counting 4 running projects the list shows · a person can run 4 unless set otherwise”, “1 of 4 · studio default”, tags “FULL · ROOM FOR 1 MORE · ROOM FOR 3 MORE”, and “Insights” twice (header + row) beside “Set capacity”. Contractors: the five project tiles PLUS four contractor tiles (FREE THIS WEEK · FREE WITHIN 7 DAYS · OVER CAPACITY · NO CONTRACTOR YET), “7 contractors · every running site counts”, “Window: This week ▾ · By contractor · By site · Vendors”, a filled “Add a contractor” beside the header’s filled “New project”, “Put on a site” on six rows, trade codes “Fittings · CV”, “Painting · CP”, names cut (“ClearView Glass & Alu…”, “AquaFlow Plumbing Wo…”), and in the drawer “Leader checked by Hui Min”.
findings.why: Words like “studio default”, “every running site counts” and “Leader checked” are the build’s, not the studio’s; nine tiles and six identical verbs bury the one contractor who is double-booked.
findings.proposal: Members: one line “Each person runs up to 4 projects · Set capacity”; the tag says “Full” / “1 free slot” (sentence case, no CAPS); drop the row’s second Insights. Contractors: hide the project tiles in this view (they describe projects, not crews); keep the four crew tiles. “Put on a site” moves into the row’s ⋮, shown as a verb only on the row that needs it; “Add a contractor” outlined; drop the two-letter codes; names wrap to two lines. “Leader checked” → “Checked by Hui Min”.

findings.area: Projects › a completed project · Complete handover
findings.title: A finished project gives three different “how long” figures and a nonsense margin line
findings.now: Shalini: brief tag “COMPLETED · TOOK 293 DAYS”; Progress “Setting up 243 days · In progress 50 days”; Closing summary “Days · 2 more than the 48 planned · 50 days”; “Margin · Margin 79% — 79 points over the expected 0%” in red; truncated “Variation orders · 1 appro… · +S$1,853”, “Costs · Committed — POs, bills a… · S$ 9,044”. Ryan’s handover sheet: “Margin 66.6% — 42.6 points over the expected 24%”.
findings.why: An owner reading “took 293 days” for a 50-day job thinks the project ran ten months late. “Points over the expected 0%” is accounting jargon and, at 0%, meaningless; a healthy margin drawn in red looks like a loss.
findings.proposal: Brief tag: “Completed · 50 days on site”. Progress keeps its stage durations. Margin warning only when the expected margin exists and is above 0, worded “Margin 79% — the quote planned 24%”, in the warning tone only when the margin is BELOW plan. Closing rows: the caption wraps instead of truncating.

findings.title: Handover sheet: “Defer” on every row, up to four purple verbs a row
findings.now: A paragraph, then a CHECKLIST card whose rows carry “Defer · Open the schedule”, “Defer · Remind”, “Defer · Send the Completion invoice · Open Money”, “Defer · Open Costs”, and the compliance row “Defer · Mark “Monitor 12-month defects…” done · Mark “Arrange MCST…” done · Open Compliance”; then a margin line, a CLOSING SUMMARY card, and the filled “Complete anyway”.
findings.why: “Defer” is not a word studios use, and four verbs per row turn a checklist into a control panel. The one decision — hand over or not — is buried.
findings.proposal: Each row: its state + ONE verb (the fix: Remind · Send the invoice · Open). “Defer” → a quiet checkbox “Leave for after handover” (or the row’s ⋮ › “Leave for later”). The two compliance marks collapse into “2 items left · Open Compliance”. Cut the paragraph to one line: “Completing locks the schedule, choices and money. An Owner or Admin can reopen it.”

findings.area: Projects › Overview info column (and the lead’s)
findings.title: “Collaborators · Owner Michelle · Members Michelle” — the role word “Owner” means someone else here
findings.now: Section “Collaborators” (with “Add”) → “Owner · Michelle”, “Members · [M] Michelle ⋮”, “Team chat · Only the team reads it · Messages”. Michelle is a Designer; Dane is the studio’s Owner. The listing’s column is “Members”; Workload says “Members · Contractors”; the portal says “Team”.
findings.why: “Owner” is the studio’s top role everywhere else (Settings › Roles & access); seeing “Owner: Michelle” on a project makes a Designer look like the owner. The same name twice adds a row of reading.
findings.proposal: Section title “Members” (the word the listing uses). Rows: “In charge · Michelle” (the lead owner) and the Members row only when there is someone besides them. “Team chat” stays as the one link.

findings.title: “Mark done” looks different in each place on the same project
findings.now: Schedule at 1440: purple outlined “Mark done” on the two running milestones only. Schedule at 390: a small purple “Done” on EVERY unfinished row, including Cleaning and Handover that haven’t started. Compliance: a grey outlined small “✓ Mark done”. Tasks: a circle to tick. The Needs you row: a purple text “Mark done”.
findings.why: Four looks for one action makes each list feel like a different app, and offering Done on a milestone that hasn’t started invites a slip.
findings.proposal: One pattern: the row’s leading circle ticks it (as Tasks) wherever an item can be done, opening the Mark done sheet for milestones; no separate button. If a button is kept, it is the DS outlined “Mark done” in every list, shown only on rows that are running.

findings.title: Seven date formats on one project
findings.now: “21 Aug ’26” (info column) · “Wed 28 Oct” (Needs you) · “Mon, 19 Oct ’26” (activity) · “Tue, 3 Nov ’26 · 10:00 AM” (Tasks, underlined) · “Thu, 30 Jul ’26 · 12:00 PM” (Meetings) · “30 Jul ’26, 12:00 PM” (Notes) · “27/10/2026”, “5/11/2026”, “27/9/2026” (the date fields in Mark done, Start the project, the milestone panel) · relative “12d ago” (Messages) and “27 days ago” (With Ryan) · listing “Sun, 29 Nov ’26” inside “On hold till:”.
findings.why: Every format change is a re-read; “5/11/2026” is ambiguous to anyone used to the app’s “5 Nov”.
findings.proposal: One rule from lib/format.ts: day-month in rows (“28 Oct”, the year only when not this year), weekday only where the day matters (“Wed 28 Oct”), time as “· 10:00 AM”, never a comma before the time; the house DateField shows its value the same way (“5 Nov 2026”) — the picker still edits it. Relative time only for under a day (“2 hours ago”), else the date.

findings.title: Money is written four ways — the same S$13,370.04 shows as “S$ 13,370” and “S$13,370.04”
findings.now: Listing “S$48,600” (no space); Overview cards “S$ 81,355” (a space, no cents — moneyCard); Money tab “S$14,018.04” (cents); listing tile “S$ 261.9K”; Needs you on the Overview “S$ 13,370” and the same row on the Money tab “S$13,370.04”; Choices “+S$420 + GST” (studio) vs “Adds S$457.80” (portal, GST in).
findings.why: Two different-looking numbers for one payment make an owner double-check; a space after S$ in some places and not others looks careless on a demo.
findings.proposal: One money style for the screen: “S$13,370.04” (no space) in rows and panels; whole dollars “S$81,355” only on summary cards; compact “S$262K” only on tiles. Choices show the same figure to both sides (“+S$457.80 incl. GST”).

findings.title: The same money step is a plain row on the Overview and a pink banner with a filled button on Money
findings.now: Woodcraft’s overdue bill: on the Overview a row with a red title and a purple text “Pay”; on the Money tab a pink alert banner with “Open” and a filled “Pay”. Ryan’s payment to confirm: text links “Confirm · See the bank’s confirmation” vs a grey banner with “See the bank’s confirmation · Not received” and a filled “Confirm”.
findings.why: Two drawings of one item ask the owner to learn two patterns, and the louder one sits a tab away from the summary.
findings.proposal: One Needs-you row component for both pages (the Overview’s row, one outlined verb, ⋮ for the rest); the Money tab’s list is that row filtered to money.

findings.title: Schedule: a red summary, a purple banner, eight toolbar controls and a legend paragraph
findings.now: Red headline “2 milestones are late. Handover is set for Fri 13 Nov.” + a two-line paragraph + three figures (“Done 2 of 7 · To handover 17 days · Next payment 30% · payment to confirm”); a purple banner “Michelle asks for more time… Open it”; toolbar “Weeks · Months · Today · ⛶ · +3 days from changes · Contractors · 2 · Ryan sees this schedule. Last shared 13 Oct. · Add milestone · ⋮”; payment pills in CAPS “30% · 21 AUG”; row statuses cut (“Blocked · waiting on the plumbe…”, “More time asked, to Wed 28 Oct · was due Wed…”, “Should have started Sat 24 Oct · No Painting co…”); and under the chart “The line marks today, Tue 27 Oct. Shaded columns are weekends. A diamond is a payment from the quote’s schedule. A line joins a milestone to what it waits on — red when it started before that one allows.”
findings.why: The timeline is the point; it starts halfway down the screen. “Next payment 30% · payment to confirm” doesn’t say how much or what to do; the legend paragraph explains the chart instead of the chart explaining itself.
findings.proposal: Fold the paragraph into the headline; move “+3 days from changes” and “Ryan sees this schedule…” into the summary card as one line; drop the banner (3-01); the legend becomes a “?” Tooltip on the chart head. Payment pills sentence case (“30% · 21 Aug”) or the diamond alone with a tooltip. Next payment: “S$13,370 to confirm”. Status lines wrap to two lines instead of “…”.

findings.title: The scope menu carries paragraphs under its rows
findings.now: “Needs attention — Overdue tasks, milestones, choices or payments; a client who says something is not right; a long wait; no recent update; a set-up that stalled” (6 lines); “Waiting on client — A quote, contract, variation order, invoice, stage or choice for them to answer; questions, designs or the portal invite not opened; a milestone that waits on them” (7 lines); “Needs my review — Updates, invoices, handovers, schedule asks, purchase orders and expenses waiting for your approval, and payments to confirm” (6 lines). Groups “TO DO · ACTIVE · INACTIVE” in caps.
findings.why: A menu is for picking; paragraphs make the owner read three essays to find “Completed”.
findings.proposal: One-line help at most (“Late, stuck or quiet”, “Waiting for the client”, “Waiting for your OK”) — the full list in the row’s Tooltip. Group labels sentence case.

findings.title: “Invite to Portal” names the panel even after the client has opened it; summaries cut off
findings.now: Title “Invite to Portal” for Ryan, whose chip reads “OPENED 9 MINUTES AGO”; the row also says “Invited 9 Aug by Michelle” (Marcus: chip “NOT INVITED” + text “Not invited yet” — the same fact twice). “Their page localhost:3303/my/demo-studio Copy”. “What Ryan can see”: “Choices · 1 said no to” (dangling), “Files · None of 10 shown”. Company calls it “Client portal”; the With Ryan card says “Portal opened 16 Oct”.
findings.why: Inviting someone who is already in reads like a mistake; “1 said no to” is a broken sentence on a page meant to reassure.
findings.proposal: Title “Client portal” (Company’s name) — the ⋮ row “Client portal…”; the button stays “Invite on WhatsApp” / “Send the link on WhatsApp”. One state per person: the chip OR the caption, not both. “1 said no to” → “1 turned down”; “None of 10 shown” → “10 files, none shared yet”.

findings.title: Money’s New ▾ is nine rows, each with a two-line explanation
findings.now: BILL RYAN: “Variation order”, “Variation order from a contractor’s quote”, “One-off invoice”, “Record an invoice made elsewhere”; COSTS: “Purchase order”, “Order from the quote”, “Record a PO made elsewhere”, “Supplier bill”, “Expense” — every row with a 2-line helper (“One raised in your accounting system or on paper — it counts in the costs”).
findings.why: Nine near-twins (two VO rows, two “made elsewhere” rows, two PO rows) and eighteen lines of help make a simple “add” a reading task; “PO” is jargon for small studios.
findings.proposal: Five rows: “Variation order”, “Invoice”, “Purchase order”, “Supplier bill”, “Expense”. The variants (“from a contractor’s quote”, “made elsewhere”, “from the quote’s lines”) become the first choice inside each dialog. Helpers go (the dialog explains).

findings.title: Choices card: three tags (one repeats the heading), truncated option names, two buttons
findings.now: Group heading “Common bathroom · 1”, then the card’s tags “COMMON BATHROOM · NEEDED BY THU 29 OCT · IN 2 DAYS · OTHER OPTIONS ASKED”; options cut to “Charcoal matte, 3…” and “Slate grey terrazz…”; the banner’s filled “Share again” + grey “Choose with Ryan”; prices “No change” / “+S$420 + GST”.
findings.why: The option name IS the decision and it is cut; the room is said twice; a filled button adds a second primary to the page.
findings.proposal: Drop the room tag (the group says it); “Needed by Thu 29 Oct” as plain caption text; one status tag. Option names wrap to two lines under the swatch. “Share again” outlined; “Choose with Ryan” into the card’s ⋮.

findings.title: Floor plan view has ~60 controls on its first screen
findings.now: Views chips; “Unit layout · Main” chip; “☆ MAIN PLAN” tag; “Add a plan · ⬇ · ⋮”; a grey banner; tools “Select · Pen · Box · Arrow · Text · Pin · Photo · Zone · Cloud · ›” + colour ▾ + “General ▾” + undo + full screen; side: “Both · Studio · Ryan”, a switch “Show resolved marks”, trade chips “Carpentry 2 · Electrical 1 · Lighting 2 ›”, “6 marks”, a POINTS card, then a card per mark (“Pin 1 · Ryan D’Souza · Client requests · 25 Aug ’26”).
findings.why: Marking up a plan with a client needs the plan and three tools; this screen asks the owner to scan five control rows first.
findings.proposal: Tools as one icon toolbar on the canvas edge (labels in tooltips, Select · Pin · Pen · Text visible, the rest under “More tools”). The side’s filters collapse to one “Show: Both · All trades ▾” pill. Drop the MAIN PLAN tag when there is one plan.

findings.title: Compliance: a summary line nobody can parse, a table head that names nothing
findings.now: “Condo · 4 items to do this phase” (the home is an Executive Condo); “6 of 10 items answered · 4 mandatory items still to do · While the works run on site · the phase this project is in”; every section is a bordered table with a grey “ITEM” head over a single column; each row has a purple “Details ▾”, a tag (DONE / NOT NEEDED / MANDATORY) and an authority (“MCST / NEA”).
findings.why: “answered” for a checklist, “the phase this project is in” and an empty table head are filler; a box per section with a one-word head is boxes inside boxes.
findings.proposal: One line: “Execution (now): 4 of 6 done · 4 required left”. Sections as plain headed lists (no table head, no card per section). “Details ▾” → the row opens on press. “Condo” → the property type the record has.

findings.title: The AI brief states a past date as current and repeats the milestone
findings.now: “Carpentry fabrication runs to 21 Oct ’26. Carpentry fabrication is the last one running.” on 27 Oct, for a milestone 6 days late (with Electrical blocked). Tag “THIS WEEK” in orange caps; heading “MAISON AI BRIEF”.
findings.why: The brief is meant to be the smart summary; a stale date and a doubled name read as a machine template and undermine trust in every other line.
findings.proposal: When the running milestone is late, say so: “Carpentry is 6 days late — Michelle asks to finish Wed 28 Oct.” Never repeat the title in one brief. Drop the orange tag (the brief is always this week) or make it a grey caption.

findings.title: The same fact appears four or five times on the Overview
findings.now: Header chips “P-2026-001” and “WHOLE-HOME RENOVATION” repeat Project info’s “Number” and “Project type”. Marcus’s “Setting up” is in the stage button, the brief tag “SETTING UP”, the card meta “Setting up for 12 days”, Progress “Setting up · current · 12 days” and Project info “Stage · Setting up”. Aisha’s hold: “On hold since 15 Oct ’26” in the brief, Needs you and Progress, with the reason quoted twice.
findings.why: Repeating facts doubles the reading and makes the page feel longer than the project is.
findings.proposal: Header keeps the title + stage button; the number and type live in Project info only. A state is said once on the page (the stage button), plus where it adds a number (Progress’s days). The hold reason appears once (the Needs you row).

findings.title: “--” repeated down the info column
findings.now: Ryan: District --, Area size (sq ft) --, Remarks --. Marcus: Target end --, Contract --, Condition --, Key collection --, Remarks --. Shalini: Scope --, Contract --, Condition --, Style --, Area size --, Key collection --, Remarks --.
findings.why: Seven dashes are seven rows to read past; they look like errors on a demo.
findings.proposal: Hide empty rows; at the foot of each section one link “Add district, area, remarks…” that opens Edit details at that field (the house LeadFormModal).

findings.title: Questionnaire: a disabled “Ask Client” with no reason, a filled button, “question bank”
findings.now: Toolbar “Ask Client” greyed out (no tooltip); empty state “No questions yet · The studio’s question bank has 11 questions ready for this project. · [Add the studio’s questions]” (filled).
findings.why: A greyed button that won’t say why breaks the “say why” rule; “question bank” is our word, not the studio’s.
findings.proposal: Hide “Ask the client” until a question exists (or keep it with the house Tooltip “Add a question first”). Empty state: “Your studio has 11 questions ready · Add them”, the button outlined (the page’s filled button is the header’s).

findings.title: Start the project: five source cards with paragraphs, two of them disabled
findings.now: “Milestones come from”: “A quote — No quote on this project yet — make one, or upload a contractor’s quote below.” (disabled), “Drafted by Maison AI — Maison AI drafts from a quote’s lines — make a quote for this project first.” (disabled), “A schedule template — From Company › Templates › Schedules — the ready-made ones for each kind of home are there too.”, “An uploaded quote — … Reading it uses 5 AI credits, given back if it can’t be read.”, “Not now — Set it up later — the Schedule tab keeps its Start card.” Then “Picked for a Condo 3-bedder — the ready-made Condo schedule. Pick another if the job differs.”; date field “5/11/2026”.
findings.why: Starting a job should be a date and a confirm; the owner reads ten lines about options they can’t use.
findings.proposal: Show only the sources that work today; the disabled ones collapse to one grey line “Make a quote first to build from it”. Each card: a title and at most one short line. The template picker’s helper goes (the preview on the right shows the result).

findings.title: Portal bell rows stay as asks after the client answered them
findings.now: “A change to your contract to approve · VO-2 · Study lighting · +S$1,133.60 · 16 Oct ’26” — Ryan declined VO-2 on 18 Oct; “A change to your contract to approve · VO-1 …” — approved 22 Sep. “Your schedule is ready — The stages ahead and when each is planned”.
findings.why: A homeowner sees two things to approve that are already done and taps them to find nothing to do.
findings.proposal: Once acted on, the row’s title says the outcome: “You approved VO-1 · +S$3,455.30”, “You declined VO-2”. (The rows already know `seen: d.done`.)

findings.title: Portal at a desk shows eleven top tabs; the phone shows five and More
findings.now: Desk bar: Home · Schedule · Updates · Money · Choices · Designs · Floor plan · Messages · Issues · About · Files + bell + name + Sign out. Phone: Home · Schedule · Updates · Money · More (Choices · Designs · Floor plan · Messages · Issues · About · Files · Sign out).
findings.why: Eleven tabs is the busiest bar in the product, for the least technical user; the two widths teach different maps.
findings.proposal: Desk = the phone’s five + “More ▾” (the same list, a PortalMenu). Hide a section with nothing in it (Designs “No designs yet”).

findings.title: One record, two names: Tickets (studio) and Issues (client) — and Activity mixes them
findings.now: Studio tab and rail “Tickets”, “New ticket”, “T-2026-002”; the client’s “Issues”, “Report an issue”; the studio’s Activity: “Shalini Menon reported an issue on their portal: T-2026-003”. Status “IN PROGRESS” on a ticket reuses the project stage word. On the portal dock, Updates uses a chat-bubble icon while Messages (in More) uses another bubble.
findings.why: When a client says “I raised an issue”, the owner has to translate; “In progress” on a ticket inside an “In progress” project blurs two states.
findings.proposal: Pick one word for both sides — “Issues” reads plainer for homeowners and studios (rail “Issues”, “New issue”, “I-2026-002”); or keep Tickets studio-side but say “ticket” in Activity too. Ticket status “Being fixed” instead of “In progress”. Portal: Updates gets a newspaper/notes icon, Messages keeps the bubble. (REG H-Q2 decided the two names — flagging the cost.)

findings.title: Listing tiles: grey CAPS tiles that ignore the scope, unlike the Dashboard’s calm cards
findings.now: Four grey tiles with CAPS labels + a fifth “CONTRACT VALUE S$ 261.9K · Open projects” with no box; the same tiles stay on Workload, Contractors (with four more) and on “Completed (1)”, where they still count open projects. The Dashboard’s Pulse (calm pass, REG-3017…) draws the same StatTile as white cards with one caption.
findings.why: Same piece, two looks; tiles that don’t follow the list they sit on mislead (Completed shows “In progress 3”).
findings.proposal: One StatTile look across modules (the Dashboard’s `look="card"`), all five boxed; tiles hide on Workload / Contractors and on a stage scope where they don’t apply (or recount for the scope).

findings.title: Five count formats on the same pages
