findings.now: “Open projects (4)”, “Open (1) · Resolved and closed (0) · All (1)”, “All (7) · Payments (3)” (portal) · “Needs you · 12”, “Choices · 1”, “Contractors · 2”, “Payment stages · 4”, “Upcoming · 1” · “Needs you 4” (no separator) · red badges on tabs “Schedule 2 · Design 1 · Money 4” · “Carpentry 2” (trade chips).
findings.why: Inconsistent counts look unfinished and some — “(0)” — are pure noise.
findings.proposal: One format: a muted “· 4” after the label; never a zero (“Resolved and closed (0)” → “Resolved and closed”); red badges only on the rail and the tab strip for things waiting on you (as now).

findings.title: Title Case and sentence case alternate on the same menus
findings.now: Projects ⋮: “Export all as… · Deleted Projects · Projects Settings”; project ⋮: “Edit details · Open the lead’s record · … · Duplicate project · Copy Link · Complete handover · Delete”; Filters “Clear All · Done”; Deleted Projects “Empty Trash · Restore · Delete Forever”; “Invite to Portal”, “Contact Log”, “Add Task”, “New File”, “New Meeting”, “Ask Client”, “View Client Info”.
findings.why: Mixed case on adjacent rows looks sloppy and slows scanning; the house rule elsewhere is sentence case.
findings.proposal: Sentence case everywhere: “Deleted projects”, “Project settings”, “Copy link”, “Clear all”, “Empty trash” (better “Delete all forever”), “Delete forever”, “Contact log”, “View client info”. (Several come from the Leads mocks — Vicky’s call to update them together.)

findings.title: Template card: shorthand settings and three purple actions on every quote
findings.now: Eyebrow “TEMPLATE”, “Default Quote PDF” + “V1” + “DEFAULT” tags, “By trade › room · Default: 10/30/30/30 · Valid 30 days · GST · signs online”, “Starts with Hacking Works · Masonry Works · Carpentry Works · Plumbing Works · Electrical Works · Painting Works”, then “Change · Edit template ✎ · Save as new template”. Shown on Draft, Sent and Signed quotes alike. The same action is “Save as new template” here, “Save as Template” in ⋮, “Save as template” as the dialog title.
findings.why: The shorthand line is the template’s defaults — already applied when the quote was made; reading it on every quote is noise. Three text actions on a card that most quotes never change.
findings.proposal: One line: “Prints with Default Quote PDF (v1)” + one text button “Change”. Edit template and Save as template live in the header ⋮ (named once: “Save as template”). Hide the card’s actions once the quote is signed.

findings.area: Editor headers (quote, contract, preview, library editors)
findings.title: Header tags in capitals repeat the status pill and the title
findings.now: Quote: tags “OM-10001”, “VERSION 1”, “DRAFT”, “CONTRACT · DRAFT” next to a “Draft ▾” pill (the status twice). Contract: “FROM TEMPLATE”, “SIGNED 8 AUG ’26” next to “Signed ▾”. Payment schedule editor: “10/30/30/30”, “STUDIO DEFAULT”, “DEFAULT ON 4 QUOTE TEMPLATES”. Schedule editor: “7 MILESTONES”, “1 SCHEDULE STARTED FROM IT”. Contract template: “TEMPLATE”, “USED BY 4 CONTRACTS”. Quote template: “PUBLISHED V1”, “DEFAULT”.
findings.why: Capitals read as alarms; a status said twice and facts like “From template” or “Template” on a template add nothing to the task.
findings.proposal: Keep the status pill only. Number and version become the title’s grey subtitle (“OM-10001 · v1”); the contract link stays as one sentence-case chip (“Contract: Draft ›”). Drop “From template”, “Template”, usage counts and the split from headers (they live on the gallery card). MetaChip text in sentence case, never `text-transform: uppercase`.

findings.area: Lists and tables in Quotes, Price book, Templates
findings.title: Defaults and placeholders repeated down every list
findings.now: Tools › Quotes: the Due column is seven identical purple calendar_add_on icons (Signed quotes too); “Shared”/“Private” under every number; the title “Whole-home renovation” on every row. Price book: Status “Approved” on every row but one, Vendor “--”. Templates cards: “Not used yet”, “Not a default anywhere”, “No schedule started from it yet” on nearly every card. Items table: DISCOUNT “0%” and GST (%) “9” on every line; an eye icon after every child line’s name in its default Visible state (cutting the name: “Kitchen carpentry, top and b…”); a “SECTION” tag on every section row; an eye in four column heads.
findings.why: The eye has to skip the same token on every row to find what differs; the one quote that needs a follow-up date or the one item that is Proposed is lost.
findings.proposal: Show only exceptions: Due cell empty until hovered (the icon appears on row hover/focus) and no Due on Signed/Confirmed quotes; drop Shared/Private (see 4-15); Price book status as a “Proposed” chip in the name cell, no Status column; Vendor cell blank, not “--”; card usage line only when used (“Used by 6 quotes”); Discount and GST (%) columns hidden by default; the line eye only when a line is not fully shown (as top-level lines already do); no SECTION tag (the band and chevron say it).

findings.area: Quotes › list and Send for confirmation
findings.title: A quote’s “Due” is really its follow-up date
findings.now: Column “DUE” with the button “Set due date for Whole-home renovation”; the confirmation dialog: “Follow up in 3 days ▾ — Sets the quote’s Due date and adds a follow-up task for you”. The quote also has “Quote Valid Until”, and its payments have their own “DUE” column.
findings.why: “Due” on a quote reads as a payment due date or the validity; studios won’t guess it is a reminder to chase the client.
findings.proposal: Column “Follow up”; button “Set a follow-up date”; dialog helper “Adds a follow-up task for you on that day”. Keep “Due” for payments only.

findings.title: Validity is named five ways
findings.now: “Quote Valid Until” (desk field; VOs say “Valid until”), the banner “Its validity ended on 24 Sep ’26 — extend Quote Valid Until if the price still stands”, list mark “Expired 24 Sep ’26” with tooltip “… has passed — nothing is blocked; extend Quote Valid Until if the price still stands”, template card “Valid 30 days”, template field “Valid for (days)”, phone “valid until 24 Sep ’26”.
findings.why: Capitalised field names inside sentences (“extend Quote Valid Until”) read as system text; “Expired” and “validity ended” describe the same fact differently.
findings.proposal: Field “Valid until” everywhere. Banner and tooltip: “The price was valid until 24 Sep. Change Valid until if it still stands.” List chip “Expired 24 Sep” stays. Template: “Valid for (days)” both on the card and in the field.

findings.title: “Approved · Private” rows that were already sent; “Shared/Private” unclear
findings.now: OM-10008 (Vivien Lee) reads Status “Approved”, “OM-10008 · Private · Expired 29 Sep ’26”, Sent to client “2 Sep ’26”; on the phone “Expired 29 Sep ’26 · sent 2 Sep ’26 · not opened”; it counts in “Waiting on client · 3”. Every row carries “Shared” or “Private” under its number (from the mock 910:36323). Visibility is not shown or explained anywhere else.
findings.why: One row says approved, private, sent and expired at once; a studio can’t tell whether the client has the quote. “Private” to whom?
findings.proposal: Drop the Shared/Private word from the title cell (the status says whether the client has it). When a quote has gone to the client its status reads “With client” (4-04), so Approved never carries a sent date. If visibility must stay, show it only as a lock glyph with Tooltip “Only your team can see this quote”.

findings.title: Four date formats on one quote, five on one contract
findings.now: Fields show d/m/yyyy: “Quote Valid Until 7/10/2026”, “Contract date 7/9/2026”. Next to them: “Saved 6 Oct ’26”, payment due “~ 28 Sep ’26”, the contract text “7 September 2026”, the signing card “Sat, 8 Aug ’26”, the view-only page “Last changed 27 Aug” (no year), the contract and library editors “Saved 7 Sept ’26”.
findings.why: 7/10/2026 is read as July 10 by many; a studio sees one date written three ways on one screen.
findings.proposal: DateField displays the house date “7 Oct 2026” (REG-34’s d/m/yyyy came from typed dates; dates are no longer typed, REG-119). One short form “7 Oct ’26” for every other date (with the year on the view page). See 4-43 for “Sept”.

findings.title: Library editors repeat the name and wear double labels on every input
findings.now: Payment schedule editor shows the split five times: title “Default: 10/30/30/30”, tag “10/30/30/30”, tags “STUDIO DEFAULT” and “DEFAULT ON 4 QUOTE TEMPLATES”, a second row repeating “Default: 10/30/30/30 ✎”, and “4 milestones · 10/30/30/30”. Each table cell is a floating-label field under its own column head (“MILESTONE” over a box labelled “Milestone”, “SHARE” over “Share (%)”; the schedule’s “DAYS” over “Days”, “GAP (DAYS)” over “Gap (days)”). Schedule help: “Each one starts its gap in days after the one before ends; a negative gap overlaps them.”
findings.why: Every row reads twice; the screen doubles its words without adding a fact.
findings.proposal: Name once, in the header (click to rename, as the quote title does); drop the second row and the tags. Inputs in a table carry no floating label (aria-label from the column head). Schedule help: “Gap = days between one milestone and the next. Use a minus number to overlap.”

findings.title: Contract editor: title 4×, a bell that isn’t notifications, a link that sends
findings.now: The title shows in the header, again in a second row with ✎, as the document’s H1 and in the Outline. The header holds Draft ▾ · Send · Preview · a bell (“Automation”: “Remind me to follow up”, “Remind me to thank the client”) · a link icon (“Copy link — marks it Sent”) · ⋮ · ✕. A signed contract keeps the whole formatting toolbar visible and greyed.
findings.why: A bell is the app’s notifications icon; a copy icon that changes the contract’s status is a surprise. The repeated title pushes the document down.
findings.proposal: Drop the second-row title (rename from the header). Move Automation into ⋮ as “Reminders…” (or into the Send dialog, where it applies). Remove the header link icon — Copy link already sits in the Send dialog’s foot and says what it does. Hide the toolbar on a signed contract (the banner says it’s locked).

findings.title: “eSignatures” panel words are technical and point to the wrong place
findings.now: Toolbar button and panel title “eSignatures”; eyebrow “FILLABLE FIELDS”; rows “Studio signature — Your saved signature, from the quote editor”, “Studio initial”, “Client initial”, four outlined “Insert” buttons; a paragraph after the list “Place the fields where the parties sign. The client’s field is where they sign online once you send the link.”; then “BEFORE THE CLIENT SIGNS”.
findings.why: “eSignatures” and “Fillable fields” are software words; the studio’s signature is set on Your profile (S01), not in the quote editor.
findings.proposal: Button and title “Signatures”; eyebrow “Signature boxes”; “Your signature — from Your profile”; the paragraph as one line under the eyebrow: “Put a box where each person signs.”

findings.title: Send dialogs: 3-line subtitle with demo talk, link twice, a character count
findings.now: Contract: title “Send for digital signature”, subtitle “Your client reviews and signs in their browser. A one-time code confirms it’s them — demo only: no text is sent, any six digits sign it. The link opens for 7 days from when you send it.” The message box contains the raw link and a grey row repeats it; “347 characters”; a disabled “Code” box with +65. Confirmation and view-only dialogs share the pattern (“327 characters”, “241 characters”).
findings.why: Three lines in the house head break the 64px head; “demo only” sits in the studio’s real send flow; the link twice and a count no one needs add reading.
findings.proposal: Title “Send for signature” (the quote’s word). Subtitle one line: “Your client signs on their phone; a one-time code confirms it’s them.” Put the demo note and the 7-day window behind a “How signing works” Tooltip. Drop the link row (the foot’s Copy link copies it) and the character count (show it only past 900). Fold “Code” into the phone field’s prefix.

findings.title: Send ▾ rows use insider words; “Send for signature” opens a template picker
findings.now: “Send for confirmation — The client confirms the quote on a link — no signature yet” · “Send for signature — Add the T&Cs and raise the agreement to sign” · “Sent it another way — The client has it already — marks it Sent to Client, sends nothing”. “Send for signature” opens “Choose a contract template — Pick a template to start the contract from.” with “Start from the studio agreement” and “Use template”.
findings.why: “Raise the agreement” is jargon; “Sent it another way” is past tense among verbs; pressing Send and landing in a template gallery breaks the expectation.
findings.proposal: “Ask to confirm — Your client taps Confirm on a link. No signature yet.” · “Send to sign — Your client signs an agreement made from this quote.” · “Mark as sent — You sent it yourself; nothing goes out.” Picker title “Which agreement should they sign?” with the studio agreement pre-selected and one button “Continue”.

findings.area: Quotes › Send ▾ › Sent it another way
findings.title: “Sent it another way” changes the status at once, and may offer no Undo
findings.now: One press on the menu row marked OM-10006 Sent to Client immediately (no ask). When the lead can move stage the snackbar carries “Move to …” instead of “Undo” (use-quote-send.tsx:93), so a slip has no way back but the status menu — which then leaves the quote “Shared” with a client-sent date it never had.
findings.why: The page checklist: “A status set by hand that the client never saw asks first and offers Undo”. A mis-tap in a menu sends a false record to the lead’s trail.
findings.proposal: Open a ConfirmDialog: “Mark OM-10006 as sent? Nothing goes to Harpreet.” — Mark as sent · Cancel. The snackbar always keeps Undo; the lead’s next stage moves to the banner or a second snackbar action.

findings.title: Template editor: every column control at rest; the same 3 steps said twice
findings.now: Selecting Items table shows nine column cards, each with a switch, an alignment button, ← →, “Heading on the page”, a mm width and a Colour row of eight swatches — about 60 controls in one panel. The banner “Click any part of the page to change it on the right. Everything is saved as you go — press Publish when it looks right.” and the inspector’s empty state (“Click any part of the page to change it here. 1 Pick a part… 2 Change its words… 3 Press Publish…”) say the same thing. The deleted-draft bar reads “… the quotes on it would keep printing v0”.
findings.why: The owner’s own rule for this editor (template-editor-simplicity, REG-542): plain words, progressive disclosure, for an elderly studio owner.
findings.proposal: Columns as one list: name + switch per row; tapping a column opens its heading, width and colour. Keep the inspector’s three steps; drop the banner (or show it once and let “Got it” remove the inspector copy). Deleted draft bar: “This draft is deleted. Restore”.

findings.title: The galleries’ one filter pill has four names
findings.now: “Status: All ▾” (Quotes), “Show: All ▾” (Contracts, Tasks, Payment schedules), “Kind: All ▾” (T&Cs & Notes, Price book › My Items), none (Schedules, My Sections); on a phone just “All ▾”. The pill’s noun defaults to “Show” in LibraryGallery.
findings.why: Same control, same place, different word; “Show: All” doesn’t say what it shows.
findings.proposal: Name the pill by what it filters, always: “Status”, “Kind”, “Use”; never “Show”. Keep the noun on the phone (“Kind: All”).

findings.title: The same line field is “Kind” in the Price book and “Type” in the quote
findings.now: Price book column and item field “Kind” (Labour · Purchase · Design · Delivery); the quote’s Items column and Column settings “Type”. Vendor is “Vendor” in the Price book and “Vendor/Sub” in the quote’s Column settings; “Unit Price” (Column settings) vs “Unit price” (Price book); Markup shows “S$1,200.00” in the Price book and “S$60.00 (31.58%)” in the quote.
findings.why: An item added from the Price book changes its field names on the way in.
findings.proposal: “Type” in both; “Vendor” in both; “Unit price” in both; Markup shown as “S$60 (32%)” in both.

findings.title: Two sister lists name and draw the same things differently
findings.now: Quotes: column “CLIENT”, button “Create Quote”, search “Search title, number, client…”, title cell with number. Contracts: column “LEAD” for the same person, button “New Contract ▾”, search “Search title, status, date…”, no number, a “SIGNED COPY” column whose cell is the truncated file name “Interior Desig…” on every signed row. Phone cards: “Signed · signed 15 Sep ’26” (the word twice), contract subtitle “Signs OM-10009 · Interior…” cut.
findings.why: A studio jumping between Tools tiles has to relearn the table; “Lead” for a client who has signed reads wrong.
findings.proposal: Contracts: column “Client”; button “New contract ▾”; search “Search client, title, quote number…”; title cell second line “for OM-10009”; drop Signed Copy (its ⋮ › Download signed copy). Quotes: “New quote”. Phone cards: “Signed 15 Sep ’26” once.

findings.area: Quotes · Contracts · Price book (labels and menus)
findings.title: Title Case and sentence case mixed in menus; phone and desk disagree
findings.now: Title Case: “Rename Quote”, “Duplicate and Edit”, “Save as Template”, “Version History”, “Copy Link”, “Preview and Share”, “Manage Templates”, “Quotes Settings”, “Archived Quotes”, “Deleted Quotes”, “From Template”, “Import from File”, “Blank Quote”, “Add a Payment”, “Expand All”, “Clear All”, “Show Full Content”, “Copy Name”, “Mark as Optional”, “Add Sub-section”, “Create New”, “Round Prices”, “Export As”, “Additional Discount”, “Issuing Entity”, “Quote Title”, “Property Type”, “Site Address”, “General Info”, “Payment Schedule”, “Terms and Conditions”, “Additional Notes”. The phone’s section list writes the same tabs “General info · Payment schedule · Terms and conditions · Additional notes”, and menus mix “Create contract from this quote”, “Copy confirmation link”, “Share a view-only link”.
findings.why: Mixed casing makes menus look stitched together; the phone already shows the house case.
findings.proposal: Sentence case for every label, button, menu row and tab (as the phone does): “Rename quote”, “Duplicate and edit”, “Save as template”, “Version history”, “Copy link”, “Blank quote”, “Add a payment”, “Expand all”, “General info”, “Payment schedule”, “Terms and conditions”… (DS-level: a lint for Title Case in DropdownItem / Button children).

findings.title: “lines” and “items” for the same thing, counted in four formats
findings.now: Desk: tab “Items (16)”, card head “Items (16)”, sum row “Sum · 16 priced items”, totals “Subtotal · 16 items”. Phone: “Items 19”, header “16 lines · S$49,838”, Quote screen “16 lines · valid until …” then “16 lines” again above the cards, client page “19 lines · valid until…”. Elsewhere “FROM A TEMPLATE · 3 SAVED”, “BY CATEGORY · 11 ·”, “Waiting on client · 3”.
findings.why: “Lines” is a spreadsheet word; a client reading “19 lines” on their quote doesn’t know what it means.
findings.proposal: “items” everywhere (studio and client). One count format: the house Tabs count badge on tabs (“Items 16”), “16 items” in sentences. Drop the second “16 lines” above the phone cards.

findings.title: Three discount rows and a “Round Prices” link beside Total
findings.now: “Subtotal · 16 items S$45,723.00 · Discount S$0.00 · Additional Discount [% ▾][0.00] · + Add a discount · GST 9% ● · Total Round Prices S$49,838.07 · Margin · owners only 24.1% · S$11,020”, plus a per-line DISCOUNT column.
findings.why: Four places to discount with no discount on the quote; “Additional Discount” and “Add a discount” read as the same.
findings.proposal: Rows: Subtotal · GST 9% · Total (+ margin for owners). “+ Add a discount” as the only discount entry until one exists; then the named discount rows. “Round prices…” moves to the Items ⋮.

findings.title: Signature section says “Client signs online” twice and “signed on approval”
findings.now: Switch “Client signs online”; the box “Client signs online — Requested when you send · signed on approval”; under it “NRIC: Requested when you send” (italic).
findings.why: “Signed on approval” is internal (approval is the studio’s own step); the label repeats the switch.
findings.proposal: Box: “Olivia signs here when she accepts the quote online.” NRIC: “Asked when you send”. Switch stays.

findings.title: General Info: “Issuing Entity” vs “Issued by”; a helper about “Remarks field”
findings.now: “Issuing Entity” with helper “GST-Registered” (contracts and Finance say “Issued by”); Remarks helper “Prints where the quote’s template has the Remarks field” (also on VOs); “Project Ref #”, “Customer ID”, “Quote Title”; “Add a second client” floats alone in an empty half-row.
findings.why: “Entity” is a legal/system word; the Remarks helper explains the template’s internals.
findings.proposal: “Issued by” with helper “GST registered”; Remarks helper “Shows on the printed quote” (or none); “Project ref”; “Title”; put “Add a second client” as a text button under the Client field.

findings.title: Create Quote: three names for the moment, cards cut where they differ
findings.now: Button “Create Quote” → dialog “Start a quote” → phone “Who is this quote for?”. Eyebrows “FROM A TEMPLATE · 3 SAVED”, “MORE WAYS TO START”. Cards: “Blank Quote — The default template’s settings, an empty t…”, and all three templates read “Starts with Hacking Works · Masonry Wor…” (the part that differs is cut). “Draft with Maison AI — Describe the scope — we draft a categorized quote from your 10-item price book”. Upload tag “XLSX · CSV · PDF · 5 AI CREDITS”.
findings.why: Three identical truncated lines give no reason to pick a template; US spelling and “10-item” are noise.
findings.proposal: Button and title “New quote”. Card meta: what differs (“HDB 4-room · 6 sections”). “Blank quote — Start with an empty quote”. “Draft with Maison AI — Describe the work; Maison AI drafts it from your Price book.” (British “categorised” if kept). Upload tag in sentence case: “Excel, CSV or PDF · 5 credits”.

findings.title: Default quote prints “Sales Contract” on a quote the client only confirms
findings.now: Default Quote PDF heads every quote with “Sales Contract” and “CONTRACT FOR RENOVATION AND CARPENTRY WORKS AT THE ABOVE PREMISES”, prints “Gst 9%:” and a footer “Tel: … Fax: …”. The confirm page beside it says “Confirm this quote … the agreement and the signature come after.” A VO heads “Variation order VO-1 — to contract OM-10009” (a quote number called a contract).
findings.why: The client is told this is not the contract while the paper says it is; “Gst” and “Fax” read as careless.
findings.proposal: Seeded house style: heading “Quotation”, sub-heading “QUOTATION FOR RENOVATION AND CARPENTRY WORKS AT THE ABOVE PREMISES”, “GST 9%:”, drop Fax. VO heading “Variation order VO-1 to quotation OM-10009”. (Studios keep their own words once they edit.)

findings.title: Client pages say “preparing” for a sent quote; passed validity shown as current
findings.now: The view-only page of OM-10007 (already Sent to Client, validity passed 24 Sep) says “Hi Serena, this is the quote Germaine is preparing for you. It updates here as they work on it — there’s nothing to confirm or sign on this page.” The phone confirm card reads “19 lines · valid until 24 Sep ’26” after that date, with Confirm quote live and no word that it passed.
findings.why: The client reads a sent quote as unfinished, or confirms a price the studio no longer stands behind.
findings.proposal: Words by state — sent: “Hi Serena, here is your quote from Germaine. It stays up to date on this page.”; passed: “This price was valid until 24 Sep — ask Germaine if it still stands.” beside the total.

findings.title: Brand kit: paragraphs on every card and a preview that ignores the kit
findings.now: Two-line intro (“Every template starts from this kit — … A template can still differ on its own Brand tab.”), two-line helpers under “Logo and marks” and “Colours”, and beside the only preview a four-line note: “Default Quote PDF sets its own Brand ink, Brand grey and Band colours, and its own fonts, so changing those here doesn’t show on it.” “Save changes / Discard” in the header, while every other editor saves as you go. Three Qanvast SuperTrust badges (2024 · 2025 · 2026).
findings.why: The owner changes a colour and the preview does not move — the note admits it. A save button here and autosave elsewhere makes studios unsure whether work is kept.
findings.proposal: Preview a sample that follows the kit (or show the kit applied to the default template with its overrides cleared for the preview). One-line intro, card helpers removed (“PNG, JPG or SVG” stays as the dropzone’s caption). Autosave with the house “Saved” label, as the template editor.

findings.title: Gallery cards: truncated meta, raw first words, capitals and “A4”
findings.now: “Ready-made · 9 milestones · 6 …” (the weeks cut), “No schedule started from it yet · edi…”, “Not used yet · edited 15 Oct ’26 by …”, contract cards “4 headings · Contract date Dea…” (the template’s first words with its field names), T&C card “TERMS AND CONDITIONS FOR…”, tags “AT HANDOVER”, “STUDIO DEFAULT”, “DEFAULT”, “TERMS”, “NOTES”; quote card “Used by 6 quotes · A4”, payment card “Default: 10/30/30/30 · 4 milestones · 10/30/30/30”.
findings.why: Cards are cut before the useful fact; capitals and A4 add noise.
findings.proposal: One meta line per card with the one fact that tells cards apart (“9 milestones · 6 weeks”, “11 clauses”, “10/30/30/30”), a second line only when used (“Used by 6 quotes”). Tags sentence case. Drop “A4”, “4 headings”, the raw first words.

findings.title: Folders sit in three places and two tabs of one page open in different views
findings.now: Galleries draw a band titled with a checkbox “☐ Folders” above the cards; the contract template picker draws “Folders” under the templates; the Price book list draws folders as table rows; the T&Cs templates modal as rows on top. Price book › My Items opens as a table, My Sections (same page) as a grid.
findings.why: Same object, different place; the “Folders” checkbox looks like a filter.
findings.proposal: Folders always first, as rows in list view and cards in grid view; no “Folders” checkbox heading (each folder has its own box). One default view per page (list for the Price book’s both tabs).

findings.title: The contract picker draws text cards in capitals; the gallery draws pages
findings.now: Choose a contract template shows each template as an uppercase title (“INTERIOR DESIGN SERVICE AGREEMENT”) over its raw first words in grey, plus a “LAST USED” tag; Company › Templates › Contracts and the quote template picker draw the real page thumbnail.
findings.why: The same templates look different in the two places a studio meets them.
findings.proposal: Use the gallery’s thumbnail (the contract paper renderer) in the picker, title in sentence case under it, “Last used” as a sentence-case chip.

findings.title: “My Items”, “My Sections”, “My Templates” for the studio’s shared library
findings.now: Price book tabs “My Items · My Sections”; row menus “Save section to My Sections”, “From My Items · Kitchen carpentry…”; Terms / Notes cards’ link “My Templates”, whose modal is titled “Terms and Conditions Templates” with “Manage Templates” and a filled “Create New” beside each template’s “Add”.
findings.why: “My” reads personal, yet the book is the whole studio’s; the modal’s filled Create New out-shouts the action the user came for (Add).
findings.proposal: Tabs “Items · Sections”; “Save to Price book”; “From the Price book · …”; link “Templates”; modal title “Terms and conditions templates”, “Create New” as an outlined secondary.

findings.area: Price book › item dialog and Import
findings.title: Item dialog: a helper under nearly every field
findings.now: Subtitle “Lines already on a quote keep what they copied; new picks take these values.”, then helpers “The studio’s units — Settings › Quotes & pricing”, “27.27% of the cost”, “What a quote line starts at”, “The studio’s trades — Settings › Quotes & pricing”, “Who supplies it — the same product from two vendors is two items”, “A product or spec page — the line keeps it; it never prints”, “A photo shows on the card and in the Add Item box, and goes onto every line picked from it.”, “Ordered on top of the quote’s quantity, for cuts and breakage”. Import: a two-line subtitle, “The book’s own export reads back in — the sheet carries no photos”, “For rows without a vendor of their own — from Company › Finance › Vendors”.
findings.why: Eight explanations for a form of eight fields; the useful one (“27.27% of the cost”) drowns.
findings.proposal: Keep the markup % and the subtitle (one line). Unit and Trade selects end with “Manage units…” / “Manage trades…” instead of a helper. Everything else into one HelpLink “How the Price book works”. Import subtitle: “Excel or CSV, up to 500 rows.”

findings.title: "Next step" says "Open" or "View receipt" on every row of Money in
findings.now: Invoices: the invoice number is purple and the "NEXT STEP" column says "Open" on all 14 rows (24 purple text actions on the first screen). Payments: "RCT-2026-010" purple + "View receipt" on 12 rows. Variation orders and Credit notes: "Open" on every row. The help line: "Every invoice sent, and the Drafts that are ready to send, waiting for approval or sent back — a stage’s Draft joins once its milestone is reached."
findings.why: "Open" is not a next step. A column of identical purple words is pure noise and hides the few rows that need a real action (Send, Confirm, Remind).
findings.proposal: The row opens on press (it already does through its first cell). Next step shows a verb only when there is one — "Send" on a ready Draft, "Confirm" on a payment to confirm, "Remind" on an overdue invoice — otherwise empty. The record number in on-surface text, not purple. Help line → "Sent invoices and Drafts ready to send." (the milestone rule moves to a Tooltip).

findings.title: Each Finance list draws its row actions differently
findings.now: Money in: purple "Open" text, no ⋮. Money out (POs, Bills, Expenses): purple verb + bordered ⋮ box; rows with nothing to do show only the ⋮. Paid: ⋮ only, and its first column is black while every other list's is purple. Vendors: ⋮ only. Commission: the member row "Pay Germaine S$667.41" and each project row under it "Pay" + ⋮ — two Pays for one person; the asks row has two purple verbs "Decline  Approve". To do: verb + ⋮.
findings.why: The same kind of row (a money record) behaves five ways in one module; the owner cannot learn where the action is.
findings.proposal: One grammar for every Finance list, the house rule: name in on-surface text (the row opens), at most ONE verb as a DS secondary outlined small button when a next step exists, and the ⋮ always. Commission: the member row carries "Pay S$667.41"; project rows carry only ⋮ (Pay this project). Asks: "Answer" → a dialog with Approve / Decline.

findings.area: Finance › To do vs Projects › Money
findings.title: The same approval is a filled button on the project and a purple link in Finance
findings.now: PO-2026-008's approval: on the project's Money tab "Needs you" it is "Send back" (text) + "Approve and send" (filled) — four filled buttons on one screen; on Finance › To do the same row reads "Approve and send" as purple text beside a ⋮.
findings.why: One decision drawn two ways; the project screen gets four filled buttons, against the house rule of one filled button a screen.
findings.proposal: Both use the row grammar: ONE outlined verb ("Approve") + ⋮ (Approve and send · Send back · Open). Filled stays for the page's single primary (the header's).

findings.title: Integrations has four filled buttons and seven different status chip words
findings.now: Filled: "Connect a Facebook page" (left, under the text), "Generate webhook URL", "Connect Gmail" (right), "Connect Xero" (right). Status chips in CAPS: "CONNECTED", "READY", "NOT CONNECTED", "1 ACTIVE", "ACTIVE" (Gmail when connected), "WORKS WITHOUT CONNECTING", "LISTED" (Profile). The Connect buttons sit on the left on one card and the right on the others.
findings.why: Four primaries on one page means none of them is the primary; seven status words for "is it on" make the owner read each one.
findings.proposal: Every Connect is a DS secondary outlined button at the card's right, in the same place. Two status words only: "Connected" (green) and "Not connected" (grey); the website address card "Ready" → "Connected"; Webhooks "1 active" → "Connected · 1"; Calendar invites "Works without connecting" → no chip, one line "No set-up needed".

findings.title: Webhooks card is written for developers: "POST JSON", "property_type"
findings.now: "Generate webhook URLs for external systems to push leads directly into your studio. Supports any platform that can POST JSON (Zapier, Make, Typeform, Facebook Lead Ads, etc.)." · steps "Generate a URL below and paste it into your form / integration tool. When someone submits the form, a POST request is sent to the URL." · "Accepted JSON fields: name, phone, email, budget, property_type, notes, source. Also accepts common aliases like full_name, mobile, message." · caps eyebrow "NEW WEBHOOK ENDPOINT" · button "Generate webhook URL" · per-hook "Simulate a POST (demo)".
findings.why: A studio owner who uses Zapier or a Typeform needs "copy this link into your form tool"; POST, JSON and field keys are for the person who sets it up, not him.
findings.proposal: Card title "Webhooks" → "Other forms (Zapier, Typeform…)"; help "Connect any form tool: make a link, paste it into the tool, and each answer arrives as a lead." Button "Generate webhook URL" → "Make a link". Eyebrow → "New link" in sentence case. The JSON field list moves behind a HelpLink "For your developer" (a Tooltip or Drawer). "Simulate a POST (demo)" → "Try it".

findings.title: "Simulated on this prototype —" sentences on every integration card
findings.now: Integrations: "Simulated on this prototype — the Qanvast leads here are sample records…", "— nothing really arrives at this address; Simulate an enquiry plays one.", "— leads from Facebook don’t really arrive…", "— no inbox is really read…", "— nothing is sent to Xero."; Meta card "The platform opens Meta’s login; the prototype connects a stand-in page."; "Simulate an enquiry arriving (demo)". Profile › Listed on Qanvast: "Simulated on this prototype — your application is kept here and isn’t sent to Qanvast; while it waits you can play Qanvast’s answer." Plan & billing: "Visa ending 4242 · expires 08/28 (demo)" and "Paid through Dodo Payments. In the live app, updating the card opens Dodo’s billing page in a new tab." (Deliberate — S34 registry of stand-ins.)
findings.why: These are developer notes. In a client demo they tell the studio the page is fake, and they add a line of grey text to every card; "Dodo Payments" is a vendor name the studio never needs.
findings.proposal: Keep the registry (lib/services/registry.ts) but render its words only for developers (behind OPENMAISON_DEV_PREVIEWS) or as one quiet "Demo" MetaChip with the sentence in its Tooltip. Billing: "Visa ending 4242 · expires 08/28" and "Update card"; drop the Dodo sentence.

findings.title: Every Settings module opens with 3–5 lines of signposts before the first setting
findings.now: Each module repeats its tab as an H2 ("Roles & access", "Lead management", "Finance"…), then a help sentence ("Applies to every lead in Demo Studio — the table, the kanban board and imports."), then "Kept in Company: Integrations · Questionnaire · Members", then "Your own details, signature and notifications: Your profile", then pointer paragraphs ("Who sees which leads — and each lead’s project, quotes and contracts — is set under Roles & access › Who sees leads.", Finance's "How a client pays — the bank and PayNow — the issuing entities and the GST switch are kept on Profile…", Projects' two). On a 390 phone this fills the first screen (Settings › Lead management).
findings.why: The signposts exist because one subject lives in two homes (Settings and Company); the owner pays for that split with a screen of words on every module.
findings.proposal: Drop the H2 that repeats the selected tab. Keep one help line. Fold "Kept in Company" and "Your profile" into one line of text links at the module's END under "Related: Members · Profile · Your profile". Delete the pointer paragraphs — the card that a pointer names gets a HelpLink inline where it matters (e.g. Who sees leads beside the lead stages), and ⌘K finds the rest.

findings.title: Three ways to save on settings-like pages, and seven different Save labels
findings.now: Header "Discard / Save changes" (Profile, a member's public profile); per-card "Discard / Save …" with its own words — "Save the numbers", "Save invoice rules", "Save the paper" (twice), "Save cost rules", "Save numbering" (Projects and Quotes), "Save rate" (outlined), "Save" (Meetings deal score, Portal welcome line, Portal privacy links, Profile › About); and save-as-you-go with a snackbar (Lead management, Roles & access, Notifications channels, Portal sections, Members). Profile has BOTH the header bar and the About card's own Discard / Save.
findings.why: The owner cannot tell whether a change is kept: on one card it saved the moment he toggled, on the next it waits for a button with a different name.
findings.proposal: One rule: a switch, chip or select saves as it changes with an Undo snackbar (already the house way on Lead management); a card of text fields gets one "Discard · Save" pair whose primary is always "Save". Profile: one sticky header pair for the whole page, the About card's own pair removed.

findings.title: The period is picked three different ways, with three different option lists
findings.now: Reports › Leads, Projects, Meetings, Studio health: Chips "Last 30 days · Last 90 days · Last 12 months · All time" + a grey line "Filtering on lead created date · 30 leads in range". Reports › Finance: a labelled select field "Period / This year" (This month · Last month · This quarter · Last quarter · This year · Last year · All time). Plan & AI credits › Usage: a ScopePill "Period: This month ▾" + "9 Oct – 8 Nov".
findings.why: Same job, three controls and two vocabularies (rolling days vs calendar periods) inside the same Company section.
findings.proposal: One ScopePill "Period: Last 90 days ▾" (PortalMenu, menuitemradio) on every report and on Usage, at the toolbar's start, with one list: This month · Last month · Last 30 days · Last 90 days · This quarter · Last quarter · This year · Last 12 months · All time. Drop the "Filtering on …" line; the pill names the period and a Tooltip says what the date is.

findings.title: Ten report chips in one row, above a period select and Export
findings.now: Chips "Profit and loss · Owed to you · You owe · Profitability · Cash flow · GST · Vendor spend · Expenses · Commissions · Client statement" (the phone already uses a select). Sub-report switches also sit above Reports › Leads ("Response time · Sales") as chips that look exactly like the range chips under them.
findings.why: Ten equal chips give no starting point and look like filters; on Leads two rows of identical chips do two different jobs (which report vs which period).
findings.proposal: Use the phone's pattern at every width: one ScopePill "Report: Profit and loss ▾" (PortalMenu with each report's help line as the row's second line) followed by the Period pill. Leads: "Report: Response time ▾". Rename "Commissions" → "Commission" (the Finance tab's word), "Owed to you" → "To collect", "You owe" → "To pay".

findings.title: Sales is seven tables and a chart on one 4,816 px page, half of it zero rows
findings.now: By team member · Where leads stop · By source (12 rows, 9 of them "0 · 0% · S$0.00 · --") · Open pipeline · Over time (chart + table) · Going quiet · Going quiet, by team member, then a 4-line foot note ("Conversion counts the leads that reached Won. Won value is the signed quote as signed, or the value agreed, before GST — variation orders are changes to a contract, never the sale; where a won lead has neither…").
findings.why: The owner wants "who sells, where leads come from, what is stuck"; rows of S$0.00 and two "Going quiet" tables bury those three answers.
findings.proposal: By source shows sources with leads that went somewhere; the rest fold into "+ 9 sources with no wins yet" (a text button). Merge the two Going quiet tables (one table, a "By member" Chips switch). The foot note becomes a HelpLink "How these are counted" opening a Tooltip / Drawer. Over time: chart only, "Show the numbers" already exists.

findings.title: Studio health is a wall of 15 number tiles, with insider names
findings.now: Four tile rows (Your team · New work · Work done · Your clients) = 15 tiles: "ACTIVE MEMBERS 8 of 9 · 1 did nothing", "SIGN-INS 188", "AI RUNS 6 · 70 credits used", "HANGOUT CHATS 2 · at 1 Hangout", "PORTAL SIGN-INS 7"…, then a chart, a member table, and a foot note. Tab is "Studio health"; Company panel says "Reports — Leads, projects and money".
findings.why: Fifteen same-weight numbers have no story; "AI runs", "Hangout chats" and "did nothing" are insider or blunt words for a page the owner may show his team.
findings.proposal: Keep four tiles (Active members · Leads added · Quotes sent · Portal sign-ins) and the member table; the rest behind "Show all figures" (a text button) or into the table's columns. Rename "AI runs" → "AI uses", "Hangout chats" → "Qanvast Hangout chats", "1 did nothing" → "1 not active in this period".

findings.area: Company › Client portal · Reports › Meetings · Settings cards
findings.title: Card heads drawn two ways in Company: bold sentence case vs grey CAPS caption
findings.now: Members, Profile, Integrations, Questionnaire, Settings and most of Reports: bold 16 sentence-case card titles ("People and roles", "Company details", "Lead stages"). Client portal › Set-up uses the lead Overview's caps caption head for every card: "GETTING IT LIVE", "WHAT CLIENTS CAN SEE", "WELCOME LINE", "PRIVACY AND TERMS", "WHAT A CLIENT SEES", "CLIENTS". Reports › Meetings mixes both on one page: "By team member" / "Objections" bold, "COACHING" / "DEAL SCORE CHECK" caps. Inside Settings cards, more caps eyebrows: "HOW LEADS MOVE", "MONEY IN", "MONEY OUT", "COMMISSION", "PAYMENT SCHEDULES AND SPLITS", "VARIATION ORDERS ARE BILLED", "ACCENT COLOUR", "ON THE PAPER", "PREVIEW · A SAMPLE INVOICE", "WHO CONFIRMS A CLIENT’S PAYMENT", "ALSO IN THE NUMBER".
findings.why: Same kind of card, two looks, sometimes on one page; caps everywhere make each card shout and add a third type style.
findings.proposal: Company, Settings and Reports cards all use the Company card head (bold title + one help line). The lead Overview's caps head stays on the lead and project Overview only. Inside a Settings card, a sub-group label is sentence-case semibold 14 ("How leads move", "Variation orders are billed"), never caps; Settings' module-level "MONEY IN / MONEY OUT / COMMISSION" become section titles in the same bold style, or go (the cards already say it).

findings.title: Tags in CAPITALS that are not statuses
findings.now: Members: "YOU", "ON THE ABOUT PAGE", "CLOSED TO NEW LEADS". Finance › To do › Recently: "INVOICE", "PAYMENT", "BILL", "PO". A member's public profile preview: "HDB & BTO HOMES", "COMPACT LAYOUTS". Questionnaire: every question's type "TEXT", "NUMBER", "DATE", "YES / NO", "MULTI SELECT". Integrations: "GOOGLE ADS (LEAD FORM)" beside a webhook name. Vendors: "ACTIVE" on all 12 rows.
findings.why: Caps chips read as status; when every row has one, nothing stands out — and the real statuses (Overdue, Waiting for approval) lose their signal.
findings.proposal: Status chips stay (Paid, Overdue, Draft…). Everything else becomes secondary text in sentence case after the name or on the second line: "Dane (you)", "Invoice · HDB 5-Room — Aisha Rahman", "Known for HDB & BTO homes, compact layouts", "Short answer", "Google Ads lead form". Vendors: drop the Status column while the Active chip is selected (see the repeated-information finding).

findings.title: Finance tables cut the very fact a row is about
findings.now: Bills: PO column "PO-2026-0…" (the number itself), Due "S$1,400.00 ov…", Project "Executive Condo — Ry…". POs: Vendor "ColourPro Painting S…", amount line "incl. S$135.00 …", "S$6,033.15 ad…", status line "Accepted on the link · 15 Sep…", "An Owner or an Admin appro…", "“The drawing shows 67 point…". Expenses: "Floor protection boards for the…", "Grab to site — tile selection wi…". To do: "What to know" cut on every row.
findings.why: A cut PO number or a cut "overdue" amount forces a click to learn what the row says; the house rule (REG-212) keeps ellipsis for cells whose width is the design — these are the key values.
findings.proposal: Let the second line of a cell wrap to two lines (no ellipsis on status lines, amounts or reasons). Give the PO column a floor that fits "PO-2026-001". Shorten the Project column to the client's name ("Shalini Menon") with the project type in a Tooltip — it is the part people recognise.

findings.title: The Project column is written four different ways
findings.now: Money in: "P-2026-003 · HDB 5-Room …" over "Aisha Rahman". Money out / To do: "BTO 4-Room — Shalini …" on one line. Profitability: "BTO 4-Room — Shalini Menon · P-2025-001". Commission: "HDB 5-Room — Benjamin Han" over "P-2026-002".
findings.why: The same project looks different on every tab, so the eye cannot scan for it.
findings.proposal: One cell everywhere (a shared ProjectCell): client name on line 1 ("Shalini Menon"), "P-2025-001 · BTO 4-Room" on line 2 in secondary text.

findings.title: Each Finance tab has a different toolbar, and counts sit on some chips only
findings.now: To do: search · chips with counts ("All · 18", "To approve · 4") · New ▾ (filled). Money in: search · kind chips without counts · "Status: All ▾" · Export (no New). Money out: search · kind chips without counts · "Status: All ▾" · New ▾ (filled) — no Export. Vendors: search · chips with counts ("Active · 12", "Contractors · 7", "Inactive · 0", "All · 12") · New vendor (filled). A "Reports ›" text link sits in the page header on every tab.
findings.why: Four tabs of one section, four toolbars; "Inactive · 0" offers a choice that shows nothing.
findings.proposal: One toolbar order on every Finance tab: search · kind Chips (no counts) · Status pill · (spacer) · Export (outlined) · New ▾ (the one filled). Vendors: "Active · Contractors · Inactive" chips without counts; hide Inactive while it is empty; drop "All".

findings.title: Kind chips and the list titles under them use different names
findings.now: Chip "Bills" → list title "Supplier bills"; chip "Paid" → title "Payments out"; Money in chip "Payments" → first column "Receipt". To do's "Stuck" section ("2 waiting on someone else"). Settings names the money-out card "Costs" and Roles & access points to "Finance › Costs", while Finance's tab is "Money out".
findings.why: The owner presses "Paid" and lands on "Payments out"; "Stuck" sounds like an error; "Finance › Costs" does not exist as a place he can find.
findings.proposal: Chip = title: "Supplier bills" (chip) or "Bills" (both); "Payments out" (chip and title). "Stuck" → "Waiting on others". Settings card "Costs" → "Money out" and every "Set under Finance › Costs" → "Set under Settings › Finance › Money out".

findings.title: The create button changes place, fill and verb from page to page
findings.now: "Add member" filled in the page header; "Add question" filled inside the card head; "New material" OUTLINED in the toolbar (no filled button on Materials); "New vendor" filled at the toolbar end; "New ▾" filled at the toolbar end; Integrations "Generate webhook URL" filled mid-card; Profile "+ Add an entity" / "+ Add an award" text buttons.
findings.why: The owner cannot predict where "make a new one" is, or which button is the page's main one.
findings.proposal: The page's create is always the one filled button at the toolbar's end (or the page header when the page has no toolbar), verb "New <thing>" for records and "Add <thing>" for people and rows inside a form: "Add member", "New question", "New material" (filled), "New vendor", "New ▾".

findings.title: Each question row has five controls plus two switches; types in system words
findings.now: 11 rows × (drag handle · up arrow · down arrow · pencil · bin) + Required switch + Active switch = 78 controls on the screen. Types as CAPS chips: "TEXT", "NUMBER", "DATE", "YES / NO", "MULTI SELECT". Help: "Customise the questions homeowners answer about their project. New leads start with the active questions; an older lead adds them from its Questionnaire tab. Ask the client sends the lead’s questionnaire to the portal."
findings.why: Drag and arrows do the same job; the bin and pencil on every row double the visual weight; "homeowners" and "client" in one paragraph; "Multi select" is a developer's term.
findings.proposal: Row: drag handle · question (press = edit) · type as secondary text · Required · Active · ⋮ (Edit · Move up · Move down · Delete). Types: "Short answer", "Number", "Date", "Yes or no", "Pick one", "Pick several". Help → "The questions every new lead starts with. Ask the client sends them to the client's portal."

findings.title: Lead preferences dialog repeats "Select a priority to configure" four times
findings.now: Title "Lead preferences · James"; intro "Select the types of leads you prefer for each category, then set how important each one is. Must match means you strongly prefer those leads. Nice to have gives a soft boost. Leave a category as Don’t care to skip it. This is optional — if not set, every factor counts equally."; under each of four categories "This category won’t affect lead matching. Select a priority to configure."; footer count "0 of 4 categories configured"; select default "Don’t care".
findings.why: The dialog is about James but says "you prefer"; "configure", "factor" and "lead matching" are system words; the same sentence four times is noise.
findings.proposal: Title "James’s lead preferences". Intro one line: "What kind of leads suit James? Leave a row on Any if it doesn’t matter." Priority options "Any · Nice to have · Must match"; drop the per-row sentence (the "Any" value says it) and the "0 of 4 configured" count.

findings.title: Lead management speaks system: "Linear / Flexible", "Raise an untouched lead"
findings.now: How leads move: "Linear — Stages are completed one at a time. Changing a lead’s stage opens the Move stage window…" / "Flexible — … Stage details can be added later from the lead’s journey." Untouched leads: field "Raise an untouched lead after" and help "A New lead with no contact logged is raised as “untouched” after this delay — to the members on it, in the bell and on the channels Notifications sets for it." Lead sources help ends "Not set yet — these are the defaults."; Lost and On Hold reasons "These are the defaults."; "Contacts expected first". Source chips carry an eye-off icon or ✕ with no words. Stage table column "LEADS NOW".
findings.why: "Linear" is an engineering word; "raised" is an alert system's verb; "Not set yet" sounds like something is wrong.
findings.proposal: "Linear" → "One stage at a time"; "Flexible" → "Any stage, any time"; "the lead’s journey" → "the lead’s stages". Field → "Mark a new lead untouched after"; help → "A new lead nobody has contacted is flagged after this time, to the members on it." Drop "Not set yet — these are the defaults." / "These are the defaults.". "Contacts expected first" → "Contacts logged first". Chip icons get Tooltips "Stop offering" (eye-off) and "Remove" (✕). "Leads now" → "Leads".

findings.title: "What waits for an Owner or an Admin" and three pointer lines repeat each other
findings.now: Card title "What waits for an Owner or an Admin" + help "Every approval a project can wait for, in one place. On, a Designer’s or a Manager’s step waits until an Owner or an Admin approves it; theirs goes at once. Off, the project’s team goes ahead." Rule "Handover needs an owner’s review" (lowercase owner, while every other rule says "an Owner or an Admin"). Pointer lines: "Whether a Designer’s or a Manager’s handover waits for an owner’s review is switched under What waits for an Owner or an Admin, above." / "Whether a milestone’s Done and schedule changes wait for an Owner or an Admin is switched under What waits for an Owner or an Admin, above." / Finance: "Whether a Designer’s or a Manager’s invoice waits for an Owner or an Admin is set with the studio’s other approvals, under Projects › What waits for an Owner or an Admin."
findings.why: A long card name repeated in three sentences that only say "see above"; "owner" vs "Owner" reads like a different person.
findings.proposal: Card title "Approvals"; help "Turn on to have an Owner or Admin approve what Designers and Managers do." Rule "Handover needs an owner’s review" → "Handover needs approval". Delete the three pointer lines.

findings.title: Settings › Finance: 5,189 px of long help paragraphs and a Save per card
findings.now: Document numbers help: "How the studio’s invoices, receipts, credit notes, purchase orders and tickets are numbered, each under its own prefix. The prefix is letters and digits, up to 8; a blank next number continues from the highest given; the digits pad the number — 3 prints 004; the year adds the year it is numbered in. Documents already numbered keep their numbers." Then Invoices, Invoice paper (with a full sample invoice), Client payments ("Trust the client’s proof"), Credit notes, Costs ("A bill over the limit below with no PO, or one that takes its PO’s bills over the PO by more than the tolerance below, waits in To do before it is paid…"), Expense categories ("…Not set yet — these are the ones every studio starts with."), The purchase order paper, Commission — each card with its own Discard / Save.
findings.why: Each rule is explained in a paragraph before the control; the owner scans eight screens to change one number.
findings.proposal: Help lines at one sentence: Document numbers → "How invoices, receipts, credit notes, POs and tickets are numbered." (the prefix/digits rules move to each field's helper, which already exist on Projects). Costs → "When POs, expenses and bills need an Owner’s or Admin’s OK." "Trust the client’s proof" → "Count a client’s proof of payment before you check it". Drop "Not set yet — …". Group the two paper cards under one "Printed papers" card with Chips Invoice · Purchase order.

findings.title: Profile helpers show template field codes and demo notes
findings.now: Company details help "What the templates print through their fields — {studio_name}, {studio_uen}, {studio_address} and the rest."; Tagline "Prints where a template places {studio_tagline} — a cover, a footer."; Social links "Handles or links, as you want them printed — e.g. @demostudio.sg. {studio_social} prints the filled ones in a line; the Social links element on a template prints each with its mark."; Listed on Qanvast "Listed before your studio used OpenMaison — what Qanvast shows isn’t on record here yet." + the Simulated line; GST "GST-registered · off turns GST off on quotes raised under it".
findings.why: Curly-brace field codes are template-editor internals; the owner just wants to type his company details.
findings.proposal: Company details help → "These print on your quotes, invoices and contracts."; Tagline → "A short line for your quote cover or footer."; Social links → "As you want them printed, e.g. @demostudio.sg." (the field codes go to the template editor's Insert field menu, where they already are). GST switch helper → "Off: quotes under this company have no GST."

findings.title: Profile is six cards on 3,743 px with two save bars
findings.now: Company details (13 fields + social + review link) · Registrations & accreditations (a five-row table with switches) · Listed on Qanvast · Issuing entities & bank details · About the studio, for clients (year, rich text, awards, photos, its own Discard / Save) · a Brand kit door. Header "Discard / Save changes" plus the About card's own "Discard / Save".
findings.why: Everything about the studio on one scroll; two save bars on one page leave the owner unsure which one keeps what.
findings.proposal: Give Profile a tab strip on CompanyShell (as Plan and Client portal have): Details · Bank & entities · Registrations · About page. One header Save per tab. The Brand kit door goes (it lives in Templates and ⌘K finds it).

findings.title: Client portal set-up says things twice: "See it as Ryan" ×2, PDPA ×2, two Saves
findings.now: Header: "LIVE" chip · "Pause the portal" · filled "See it as Ryan"; the Getting it live list also ends "Try it yourself … See it as Ryan". Step "Privacy notice — Clients sign in with their mobile number, so Singapore’s PDPA asks you to tell them how you use it — link your privacy notice. Add the link" and the card "PRIVACY AND TERMS — Clients sign in with their mobile number, so Singapore’s PDPA asks you to tell them how you use their details. Link the pages on your own website…". The Welcome line and Privacy cards each have their own filled Save. The Clients card on Set-up repeats the Clients tab. Tab "Set-up" (hyphenated).
findings.why: The same sentence and the same button twice on one screen.
findings.proposal: Header: "See it as Ryan" outlined (the checklist keeps its link) or the reverse; the Privacy notice step's "Add the link" scrolls to the Privacy card, with no paragraph of its own; drop the Clients card from Set-up (the tab exists); tab "Set-up" → "Set up". One Save per card stays only for text (see the saving finding).

findings.title: "Nothing yet", "No limit" and "—" repeated down the By member table
findings.now: 9 rows: 8 × "Nothing yet" under an empty bar, 9 × "No limit ▾" select, 9 × "—" status, 8 × "0". Help "A monthly amount keeps one person from using the studio’s month. Every active member is listed." Column "MONTHLY AMOUNT"; pill "New members: No limit ▾".
findings.why: A table of placeholders; the one row that matters (Dane, 20 credits; Sarah capped at 600) is lost.
findings.proposal: Show members who used credits or have a limit; fold the rest into "7 members haven’t used AI this month". "Monthly amount" → "Monthly limit", values as text with the select on the row's ⋮ ("Set a limit…"); drop the Status column unless someone is at their limit. Help → "Set a monthly limit so one person can’t use up the studio’s credits."

findings.title: Commission explains its rate rule in one sentence; "You" here, "Dane" on To do
findings.now: By member help: "Each member, then their projects — the share, the rate that applies (a member’s on the project, the project’s, the member’s, then the studio’s), earned before GST from the payments that count. The rules are in Settings › Finance." The signed-in member is "You … Pay yourself S$228.83" here, but "Dane … Pay Dane" on Finance › To do. Section "Asks for another rate" + status "WAITING FOR AN ANSWER". Payments section "A reversed payment stays on the record and counts for nothing."
findings.why: The rate-precedence rule is a developer's description; the same person is named two ways a tab apart.
findings.proposal: Help → "Each member’s commission, project by project, before GST." with the precedence rule in a Tooltip on "Rate". Use the name everywhere with "(you)" — "Dane (you) · Pay S$228.83". "Asks for another rate" → "Rate requests"; status "Waiting for your answer". Payments → "Commission paid"; help → drop.

findings.title: Company panel help lines cut on 8 of 11 rows; three words for "waiting"
findings.now: Rows show a help line that is truncated: "People, roles and who reports to w…", "Brand kit, quotes, co…", "My Items and My S…", "Your own finishes for the AI Visualiz…", "Your plan, the AI credits the team u…", "The page your clients sign in to — it…", "Purchase orders, …", "Leads, projects and money, for the …", "Qanvast, the website form, Meta Le…". Badges: "1 awaiting" (Templates), "1 proposed" (Price book), "4 to approve" (Finance); the rail's accessible name "Company (6 awaiting approval)".
findings.why: A help line that cannot be read is noise; three words for the same "needs your OK" make the owner wonder if they differ.
findings.proposal: Drop the help lines (names are plain; the full line can be the row's Tooltip), which also shortens the panel. One badge word: "n to approve" on all three.

findings.title: A member is also "team member", "person", "Your team"; a client a "homeowner"
findings.now: Members page / "People and roles" card / Reports "By team member" (Leads, Projects, Meetings, Health) / Commission and Plan "By member" / Health "Your team" / Settings "the studio’s team" / Workload "each person". Clients: Questionnaire "the questions homeowners answer", Integrations "Homeowners find your studio on Qanvast", Notifications "a homeowner’s chat at the tables"; everywhere else "client".
findings.why: Two names for one thing makes the owner wonder whether they are two things.
findings.proposal: "Member" for a studio person everywhere ("By member" on every report; "People and roles" goes). "Client" for the studio's customer everywhere in the studio app; "homeowner" stays only on Qanvast-facing words (Qanvast Ops, Hangouts) where Qanvast says it.

findings.title: Item table says each row's status three ways, plus '--' everywhere
findings.now: Each row carries a coloured left bar, the card head a legend ('● only in yours ● only in theirs ● no price given'), a STATUS column chip in capitals ('MATCHED', 'ONLY IN YOURS', 'ONLY IN THEIRS', 'NO PRICE GIVEN'), and the Flo Design cell says 'No price given' again on the same row. 'Difference' shows '--' on 10 of 24 rows (phone cards: 'Difference · --'). Item names cut ('Kitchen carpentry, top and bot…', 'Plumbing works, kitchen and …'). The count is in the header chip '24 ITEMS COMPARED' and again in 'Item by item  24 compared'.
findings.why: Three signals for one fact and a column of dashes make a 24-row table read like 70 things; the cut item names are the one thing the owner needs to recognise a line.
findings.proposal: Keep the Status chip, in sentence case ('Only in yours'); drop the left bar and the legend. A row with no price leaves Difference blank (no '--') and says 'No price' once, in the theirs cell. Drop the header chip '24 ITEMS COMPARED' (the card head says it). findings.area: Tools › Floorplan to 3D Isometric · 3D Space Planner · ⌘K

findings.title: Snackbars that say nothing specific
findings.now: “Successfully Created” (new lead, also Qanvast Ops), “Successfully Updated” (edit), “Lead returned successfully”, “Members updated”.
findings.why: Title Case and no subject; the house snackbars elsewhere name the thing (“Moved to Met”).
findings.proposal: “Olivia Martinez added · Open”, “Changes saved”, “Returned to Qanvast · Undo”, “Members saved”.

findings.title: The card’s time means “updated” on the kanban and “created” on a phone
findings.now: Kanban: “Updated 2d ago” / “Updated 11 Sep ’26” (UX audit L3 added “Updated” because a bare “2d ago” was read as the lead’s age). Phone card: a bare “2d ago” that IS the lead’s age (createdAt). Kanban meta line packs “9232 3113 · -- · Others · 46 days in Contacted” with “--” inside the sentence.
