findings.proposal: Phone card: “Added 2 days ago” (or move to the Last/Next lines); kanban: skip empty parts of the meta line.

findings.title: Phone: two search glyphs, the name twice, a FAB over the stage rows
findings.now: Listing: the top bar’s search (⌘K, all of OpenMaison) and the toolbar’s search (this list) sit 60px apart with the same glyph. Lead page: the name in the top bar and again 28px in the identity block; “View Client Info” button (the page calls her a lead); at rest the Maison AI FAB covers the LEAD STAGES card’s right edge (Contacted row’s value and chevron).
findings.why: Two identical glyphs that search different things; the FAB hides a value at rest.
findings.proposal: Toolbar search glyph only (the top bar keeps notifications/messages; global search stays in More or a long-press). Hide the identity block’s name on a phone (the bar holds it). “View details”. Lift the FAB above the first card or start it hidden until scroll.

findings.title: Two chat links in one column, named differently
findings.now: “Team chat · Only the team reads it · Messages” and (Won lead) “Portal · Opened 18 Oct ’26 · Client messages”.
findings.why: Two links to Messages with different words; “Only the team reads it” explains a word the row already names.
findings.proposal: “Team chat · Open” and “Client chat · Open” (or both as one Messages row with two links).

findings.title: Return state said twice; the return policy offered twice
findings.now: Muthu Vinay: header chip “RETURN PROCESSING” and the LEAD RETURNED card’s “Return status RETURN PROCESSING”; the brief asks to “Log loss reason” though the card shows “Reason No response from lead”. Return Lead dialog: an (i) icon button in the head and a link “Qanvast’s return policy” in the body — the same policy.
findings.why: Repetition, and an AI nudge that contradicts the record beside it.
findings.proposal: Keep the status in the card (drop the header chip while the card shows on Overview). Drop the dialog’s (i) icon — the link is enough.

findings.title: Won lead: “Open project” twice and a stage clock still running
findings.now: Filled header “Open project” and the brief’s outlined “Open project” (tag “THE PROJECT”); LEAD STAGES “Won · current · 67 days” and “80 days in pipeline” on a lead that is finished.
findings.why: Two identical buttons; a ticking clock on a closed sale.
findings.proposal: Brief drops “Open project” (keep “Summarise the project” or remove the brief on Won). Won row: “Won on 21 Aug ’26”; head “Took 13 days to win”.

findings.title: Invite drawer says “not invited” twice in one row
findings.now: Row “Olivia Martinez · 9123 4567 · Not invited yet” with a tag “NOT INVITED” beside it.
findings.why: Same fact twice.
findings.proposal: Keep the caption, drop the tag (or the reverse).

findings.title: Assign suggestion reads like a rule engine
findings.now: “Suggested · Sarah — Prefers HDB 4-Room (must match) leads. Assign to Sarah” above the list; foot “Clear All · Assign”; title “Assign Member”.
findings.why: “(must match)” is the scoring engine’s word.
findings.proposal: “Suggested: Sarah — she takes HDB 4-Room leads.” Button “Assign Sarah”; title “Assign members”; foot “Clear”.

findings.title: Credit and rank pages use clever or insider labels
findings.now: Tiles: “On the way back · 200 · Farah Isa — Qanvast approved the return and credits it once processed”; table column “Closures”; Ranking tiles “REVIEWS 5 · Written by homeowners · in 2026: 4*^”, “BOARD PINS 214”, footnotes “* SuperTrust 2027 will be based on these numbers. Find out more” and “^ This year’s reviews are counted …”; links “See every review on Qanvast”, “Ask homeowners for a review” while the header says “Request reviews”. Grey stat tiles here; the Dashboard’s are white cards.
findings.why: “On the way back” and “Closures” need decoding; footnote symbols are spreadsheet talk; two names for asking for reviews; “homeowners” vs the app’s “clients”.
findings.proposal: “Credits to come back · 200”, “Won”, drop the */^ footnotes into one help tooltip; one verb “Ask for reviews” (header) and drop the side link; “clients” (or “homeowners” everywhere in Qanvast and “clients” in OpenMaison — decide once).

findings.title: Column settings repeats a pin on every row; Filters repeats the head sort
findings.now: Column settings: paragraph “Toggle columns you want to see. Drag columns up or down to reorder them.”, “PINNED (3 COLUMNS MAX)”, and a pin glyph on all 13 rows next to the switch. Filters modal’s first tab is “Sort · Newest at the top / Oldest at the top” while the table heads Lead Name · Stage · Budget · Created also sort.
findings.why: Thirteen identical glyphs; two places to sort the same list.
findings.proposal: Pin glyph on hover / focus of a row; helper as a tooltip on the drawer title; “Pinned · up to 3”. Remove Sort from Filters (the heads sort; the kanban keeps newest-first).

findings.title: Esc pressed to dismiss a snackbar takes you off the lead
findings.now: On Olivia’s page press “Move to Contacted” (the refusal snackbar shows), then Esc: the browser goes to /leads. Esc is the registered page “Back” key (lib/keys/registry.ts:78), and with only a snackbar up nothing else claims it.
findings.why: Esc is the habit for “close this message”; losing the page (and its scroll) is a surprise.
findings.proposal: While a snackbar shows, the first Esc dismisses it; Back needs a second Esc. Or Back moves to ⌘[ / Alt ←.

findings.title: The showcase lead’s files are 12 images all named “Q-101”
findings.now: Files grid: eight identical floor plans named “Q-101” (12 in all, one folder “Kitchen”); the Overview’s FILES tiles and the contact log’s attachment show “Q-101” too. Olivia is also New with no owner but has a Last contact, a drafted quote, studio-answered questions and James’s completed tasks.
findings.why: The lead mocked as the page’s reference looks like test data in a demo (REG-343 asks for consistent demo records).
findings.proposal: Rename the seeded files (“Floor plan.jpg”, “Kitchen — existing.jpg”…) and give the lead an owner or remove the contact/quote trail.

findings.title: Every log in the list is titled “Contact log”
findings.now: List rows: “Contact log / Callback requested / 6 Oct ’26・4:42 PM”, “Contact log / Callback requested / 8 Sep ’26・3:01 PM”; the filter chip is “Contact Log”; the detail pane’s title “Contact log”. Opening New › Contact Log immediately adds a draft row “Contact log · No notes yet”. Phone: the note composer is docked at the bottom on the list (Title / Write a note… / tools / Save) and takes a quarter of the screen.
findings.why: The kind is shown as the title, so every row starts with the same two words; the outcome and the channel are what tell logs apart.
findings.proposal: Row title = channel + outcome (“Call — callback requested”), the kind as the icon only; one spelling “Contact log”. Phone composer opens from “+” instead of sitting docked.

findings.title: “Insights” opens a page called Reports
findings.now: Leads, Meetings and Qanvast Ops headers carry “📊 Insights” (and the phone icon); each opens Company › Reports › Leads / Meetings. The listing ⋮ has “Leads Settings” which opens Settings › Lead management.
findings.why: Two names for one place; the user who opens Reports from Company never meets the word “Insights”.
findings.proposal: “Reports”; “Lead settings”.

findings.title: Planned meeting: consent block, credit maths and “co-pilot” spelled two ways
findings.now: “Tell Jonathan before you start” + a quoted 55-word script + “I’ve told Jonathan about the co-pilot” + “The co-pilot uses 25 AI credits for each 10 minutes, and asks before each next 10.” + the prototype line. The tool is “Meeting Copilot” in Tools and “co-pilot” here. Checklist items are grey before the meeting starts and read as disabled.
findings.why: A lot to read before pressing Start; two spellings of the tool’s name.
findings.proposal: Fold the script behind “What to tell Jonathan” ; credits line → “25 credits per 10 minutes”; one spelling “Copilot”; checklist in normal text.

findings.title: Lead form repeats “Lead” in every label and explains the address twice
findings.now: Title “Create New Lead”; fields “Lead name*”, “Lead phone number*”, “Lead source”, “Property address” with helper “Client project address.”, “Assign member”; duplicate dialog title wraps to two lines (“A lead with this phone already exists”).
findings.why: The dialog already says it is a lead; the helper adds a third name (client project) for the same address.
findings.proposal: Title “New lead”; “Name”, “Mobile number”, “Source”, “Property address” (no helper), “Members”; duplicate title “Already in your leads”.

findings.title: Activity lines in system notation
findings.now: “You set the payment schedule of the quote “OM-10001” to 10/30/30/30.”; “You compared OM-10001 · Whole-home renovation with Flo Design’s quote in Quote X-Ray.”; filter chips “All · Tasks · Files · Notes · Stage” while lines about quotes, X-Ray and questions have no chip.
findings.why: “10/30/30/30” is the schedule’s internal shorthand; the chip set doesn’t cover what the feed shows.
findings.proposal: “You set OM-10001’s payments: 10% deposit, then 30 / 30 / 30.”; add a “Quotes” chip (or drop chips to All · Mine).

findings.title: Create Quote: caps eyebrows and software words
findings.now: “FROM A TEMPLATE · 3 SAVED”, “Blank Quote · The default template’s settings, an empty t…”, tag “XLSX · CSV · PDF · 5 AI CREDITS”, “Draft with Maison AI · Describe the scope — we draft a categorized quote from your 10-item price book” (US “categorized”).
findings.why: A first-time studio user doesn’t know what “the default template’s settings” means; caps tags shout.
findings.proposal: “Templates · 3”, “Blank quote — start with an empty list”, tag “Spreadsheet or PDF · 5 credits”, “…we draft a quote by category from your price book”.

findings.title: CAPITALS on tags and card heads that aren’t statuses
findings.now: Header “WHOLE-HOME RENOVATION”; card heads “NEEDS YOU · MY TASKS · WITH RYAN · COMING UP · PROGRESS · MONEY · RECENT ACTIVITY · MAISON AI BRIEF”; Choices “COMMON BATHROOM · NEEDED BY THU 29 OCT · IN 2 DAYS”; Workload “ROOM FOR 3 MORE”; stage menu “ACTIVE · INACTIVE”; payment pills “30% · 21 AUG”; Compliance “ITEM”. (The DS Tag and the lead card title 858:24893 uppercase by design.)
findings.why: Capitals shout; when everything shouts the statuses (PAID, OVERDUE) stop standing out.
findings.proposal: Caps only for status tags. Non-status tags (room, needed-by, project type, capacity) become plain 12px captions; card titles sentence case semibold. Vicky’s call — it changes the mocked card head.

findings.title: Notes: “Added during stage movement — view only”, mixed “Contact Log” / “Contact log”
findings.now: Read-only note head “🔒 Added during stage movement — view only”; chips “All · Notes · Contact Log”; list title “Contact log”, “Meeting log”; field “Date & Time”.
findings.why: “Stage movement” is the build’s name for the Move stage window.
findings.proposal: “From the lead’s Met step — read only”; “Contact log” everywhere; “Date and time”.

findings.title: One meeting shows two times: 2:00 PM in the list, 12:00 PM in the log and Meetings
findings.now: Notes list: “Meeting log · In person · 30 Jul ’26 · 2:00 PM”; the same log open: “Date & Time · 30 Jul ’26, 12:00 PM”; Meetings tab: “Thu, 30 Jul ’26 · 12:00 PM”.
findings.why: Two times for one meeting — the list seems to show when it was logged, the log when it happened, unlabelled.
findings.proposal: The list shows the meeting’s own time (12:00 PM); if the log time matters, caption it “logged 2:00 PM”.

findings.title: Invoice panel: “Copy the no-login link”, “None — Issue a credit note takes money off it.”
findings.now: Links “Open the invoice · Download PDF · Copy the no-login link”; empty Credit notes “None — Issue a credit note takes money off it.”; totals “Amount · incl. GST · Paid · To confirm · To pay”.
findings.why: “No-login” is a technical description; the credit-note sentence doesn’t parse.
findings.proposal: “Copy the client’s link”; “No credit notes. Issue one to take money off this invoice.”; totals “To pay” → “To collect” (3-03).

findings.title: Activity: “System” as a person, a commission ask in riddle form
findings.now: “System uploaded the file “Transfer to Demo Studio, 3 Oct.png”.”; “Michelle asked for 5% of what the client pays on the project — “Two variation orders and extra site visits on this one”.”
findings.why: “System” is our word; the commission line takes a re-read to understand.
findings.proposal: “Ryan’s bank slip was added: Transfer to Demo Studio, 3 Oct.png” (name who caused it); “Michelle asked for a 5% commission on this project — …”.

findings.title: Milestone panel: nine colour chips, two filled buttons, numeric dates
findings.now: An ask band with a filled “Approve” + “Decline”, status segmented “Not started · In progress · Blocked · Done”, “Ask Maison AI about this”, Description, “Starts 27/9/2026 · Ends 21/10/2026”, “25 days. Push it later by 1 day · 3 days · 1 week”, “Moves with”, “If electrical moves, carpentry moves by the same number of days.”, “It waits for another milestone too”, “Bar colour: By status · Blue · Green · Amber · Brown · Navy · Pink · Teal · Purple”, Tasks “Add a task · Suggest tasks”, foot “Delete milestone · Cancel · Save” (filled).
findings.why: Bar colour is a rare setting taking two rows; two filled buttons in one panel compete.
findings.proposal: Bar colour under a “More options” fold; the ask band’s Approve outlined (Save is the panel’s primary). Dates as “27 Sep 2026”.

findings.title: Deleted Projects: a banner and a paragraph saying the same thing
findings.now: Yellow banner “Deleted projects stay here until they are deleted forever.” and a foot note “Note: Deleted projects are hidden from the list and reports. Restore puts one back with its schedule, updates and money — a project made by hand brings its client’s details back with it. Only Owners and Admins restore or delete a project.”; “Empty Trash”, “Restore · Delete Forever” on each row; the Client column repeats the name already in the project title.
findings.why: Two notices and a duplicated column on a one-row table.
findings.proposal: Keep one line under the title: “Restore brings back its schedule, updates and money. Only Owners and Admins can restore or delete.”; drop the banner; drop the Client column (the name has it); Restore as the row verb, Delete forever in the row’s ⋮.

findings.title: Portal Choices: “Demo Studio has your answers” while the client is still waiting
findings.now: Lede “Demo Studio has your answers.”; section “With your designer” and the card’s tag “WITH YOUR DESIGNER”; at the foot “You asked for other options on 16 Oct … Your designer will come back to you with other options.”
findings.why: The lede reads as “all done” while the page says the opposite; the heading and tag repeat each other.
findings.proposal: Lede “Your designer is finding other options for the bathroom tiles.”; drop the tag under a section that already says it.

findings.title: A payment stage is “Mid-Project” to the studio and “Mid-project” to the client
findings.now: Studio Billing “Mid-Project” (from the Won step’s split: “Mid-Project · 50% completion”); the portal sentence-cases it to “Mid-project · 30% · 50% completion”.
findings.why: Small, but it is the same line a studio reads aloud to the client.
findings.proposal: One spelling: sentence case at the source (lib/leads/stage-data.ts) so both sides say “Mid-project”.

findings.title: Portal Files: “Open” on every row, CAPS group heads, “Agreements” for the contract
findings.now: Groups “QUOTES · AGREEMENTS · VARIATION ORDERS · PAYMENT RECEIPTS · SELECTION RECEIPTS”, each row with a purple “Open”; the studio calls the agreement “Contract” and its folder “Contract & VOs”.
findings.why: Six identical verbs where the row itself could open; a second name for the contract.
findings.proposal: The whole row opens (chevron); group heads sentence case; “Agreements” → “Contract” (or the studio side says “Agreement” — one word).

findings.title: Project hold offers “No date yet” chips the lead’s On Hold doesn’t
findings.now: Project: “Resumes · No date yet · 1 month · 3 months · 6 months · Custom” + “No resume date — resume it when the client is ready.” + “Tell Ryan on WhatsApp”. Lead On Hold (REG-453): “1 month · 3 months · 6 months · Custom”.
findings.why: Same dialog, two sets of choices — a studio that learnt one is surprised by the other.
findings.proposal: One chip set for both (add “No date yet” to the lead’s, or drop it here and let an empty Custom mean no date).

findings.title: Portal schedule: “YOU ARE HERE” on the paused milestone; invoices mixed into the steps
findings.now: Electrical (Paused) carries the “YOU ARE HERE” flag while Carpentry is “Under way”; rows “Invoice INV-2026-001 sent · Sat 8 Aug · Deposit · S$7,790.01 · Paid” sit between milestones; chips “All (7) · Payments (3) · Under way (1) · Pa…” clipped.
findings.why: Two current steps, one flagged “you are here”, confuse where the job actually is.
findings.proposal: Flag the milestone that is under way (or none when two run); show invoices only under the Payments chip; counts per 3-39.

findings.title: Stage menu: “Setting up · Started 21 Aug ’26” reads as the setting-up start
findings.now: Groups “● ACTIVE · ● INACTIVE”; “Setting up ✓ · Started 21 Aug ’26”, “In progress · current”, “Completed”, “On hold”.
findings.why: “Started” under Setting up means the works started (the move to In progress) — it reads the other way.
findings.proposal: “Setting up · done 21 Aug”; “In progress · since 21 Aug”; group labels sentence case, or drop them (four rows need no groups).

findings.title: With Client view open, the Items card loses its title; toolbar wraps
findings.now: At 1440 with the eye’s Client view pane open, the Items card head shows only a chevron — “Items (16)” is gone — and Create ▾ / full-screen drop to a second row.
findings.why: The section’s name disappears exactly when the studio is comparing it with the client’s view.
findings.proposal: Fold the toolbar the way it folds at ≤1024 (search · New section · Create ▾ · ⋮) when the card is narrower than its controls; the title never shrinks to zero.

findings.title: Upload a quote opens a 1200-wide dialog for one field and one dropzone
findings.now: The xl modal holds “Client*”, one helper line and a dropzone, then ~600px of white.
findings.why: An empty giant dialog reads as broken or still loading.
findings.proposal: Open Upload a quote at the m (600) width, height to content (the house scale).

findings.title: “Saved 7 Sept ’26” — a second copy of the Saved label drifts from the house date
findings.now: lib/contracts/model.ts:48 builds the month with toLocaleString('en-SG') → “Sept”; the quote editor’s own copy (quote-editor.tsx:118) uses displayDate → “Sep”.
findings.why: The same label reads two ways; lib/format.ts:37 already warns about exactly this.
findings.proposal: One savedLabel in lib/format.ts on MONTHS, used by the quote, contract and library editors.

findings.title: The sum row adds quantities of different units
findings.now: “Sum · 16 priced items” shows QTY “2516” — 885 sqft + 78 ft run + 46 point + Lots — and repeats the total under UNIT PRICE.
findings.why: A number nobody can use, in bold, invites a wrong reading.
findings.proposal: Leave Qty and Unit price empty on the sum row unless every counted line shares one unit.

findings.title: A space before punctuation after every field chip
findings.now: “The contract sum is S$77,900.12 , inclusive of GST…”, “(UEN UEN )”, “Dear Client name ,” on the paper, the preview and the client’s signing page.
findings.why: Reads as a typo on the document the client signs.
findings.proposal: Trim the space the token renderer adds after a resolved value (or the seeded text’s leading space) so punctuation hugs the value.

findings.title: The row’s hover View button covers the Created date
findings.now: Hovering a row parks “View” and ⋮ over the visible right edge; at 1440 they sit on the CREATED / SENT TO CLIENT cells (“10 Sep ’2…”).
findings.why: REG-446 / REG-448: a hover control never covers a value the row exists to show.
findings.proposal: Reserve the actions’ room at the table’s end (a 120px tail track), or drop the hover View — the title already opens the quote.

findings.title: An empty “IC” line prints when the NRIC is blank
findings.now: The header block prints “IC” with nothing after it on Olivia’s and Serena’s quotes.
findings.why: A blank label on the client’s paper looks unfinished.
findings.proposal: Skip a details row whose value is empty (the template keeps the row for when it is filled).

findings.title: “How fields fill in” answers with a snackbar
findings.now: The text button shows a snackbar: “Fields fill in from the lead, the quote and your studio when a contract starts from this template”.
findings.why: Snackbars report what just happened; help that vanishes in four seconds is lost.
findings.proposal: Make it the house Tooltip (or HelpLink) on the button.

findings.title: Comments drawer says it is empty twice and its button says “Submit”
findings.now: “0 Comments” then “No comments on this quote’s lines yet. Comment on a line from its ⋯ menu, or pick one below.”; composer “Chat with your team here”, button “Submit”, caption “Clients can’t see these comments”.
findings.why: Say it once; “Submit” is a form word.
findings.proposal: Drop “0 Comments”; empty line “No comments yet — pick a line below.”; placeholder “Write a comment”; button “Send”.

findings.title: Phone Preview headings in capitals; sentence case on the Quote screen
findings.now: Preview at 390 lists “MASONRY · PLUMBING · FITTINGS”; the Quote screen’s cards say “Masonry”; the client page “CARPENTRY”.
findings.why: The same heading changes case between two screens a tap apart.
findings.proposal: Sentence case (“Masonry”) for reading-card headings everywhere.

findings.title: “…an Owner or an Admin can move it back from the status” is unclear
findings.now: Signed banner: “Marked signed on 8 Aug ’26. This is the copy kept at that moment; an Owner or an Admin can move it back from the status.” + outlined “Signing record”, beside a filled “Download signed copy”.
findings.why: “Move it back from the status” doesn’t say how or why.
findings.proposal: “Signed on 8 Aug ’26 — this copy is locked. An Owner or Admin can undo the signing from the status menu.”

findings.title: A VO stacks two purple banners and quote-only words
findings.now: Banner 1 “A change to the contract of HDB 5-Room — Aisha Rahman (P-2026-003): S$62,702.25 today, S$62,157.25 once the client approves it. An omission is a line with a minus quantity.”; banner 2 “Sent to the client on 16 Oct ’26, opened 13 min ago (4 times) — they have version 1. Edits here change what they see on their link; to change the variation order and keep what they saw, revise it.” The Remarks helper still says “quote’s template”; the Template card shows on a VO.
findings.why: Two dense banners before any field.
findings.proposal: One banner, one line: “Changes HDB 5-Room — Aisha Rahman’s contract by −S$545 · with Aisha since 16 Oct.” The how-to (“minus quantity”) as a Tooltip on the Items head; hide the Template card on a VO.

findings.title: Access chip repeats the Last opened date on every row
findings.now: ACCESS "OPENED 18 OCT" chip and LAST OPENED "18 Oct" on the same row (6 rows); "--" in Invited / Last opened for others; ACTIONS column of ⋮.
findings.why: Same fact twice per row.
findings.proposal: Access chip says the state only: "Opened" (green) · "Invited" (yellow) · "Not invited" (grey); the date stays in Last opened.

findings.title: Vendors table: "POS" head, cryptic codes and a Status column of ACTIVE
findings.now: Column "POs" is uppercased by the head style and reads "POS". Captions "Plumbing · works on site · AF", "Hacking · Masonry · Tiling · works on site ·…" (AF / BS / CV = the vendor's code). Status "ACTIVE" on all 12 rows while the Active chip is on. GST "No GST / Charges GST". "--" vs "- -" in Committed / Owed.
findings.why: "POS" reads as point-of-sale; "works on site · AF" is internal.
findings.proposal: Head "Purchase orders" (or "Orders"); caption "Plumbing · Contractor" (code in the drawer only); drop the Status column when the chip already narrows to Active; GST "Charges GST / —".

findings.title: Quotes settings leak a field code, a template name and mixed-case units
findings.now: Prepared by: "What a template’s {prepared_by} field prints on every quote…". New quotes start with: "What every new quote takes from the studio’s default template, Default Quote PDF… Change in Default Quote PDF › New quotes". Units list "Pieces · Lot · sqft · ft run · point · hour · set". Selling prices "…The cost never moves; the markup takes the difference. Round Prices on a quote still rounds the whole quote at once." Contracts sits in this module as "Contracts · signing links".
findings.why: {prepared_by} is a template internal; units in two cases look like a typo.
findings.proposal: "What prints as “Prepared by” on every quote"; units "Piece · Lot · sqft · ft run · Point · Hour · Set" (or all lower case — one case); "Contracts · signing links" → "Signing links".

findings.title: The meeting tool is spelled four ways: co-pilot, Copilot, Co-Pilot, Co-pilot
findings.now: Code count: "co-pilot" 161 · "Copilot" 54 · "Meeting Copilot" 51 · "Meeting Co-Pilot" 13 · "Co-pilot" 1. Settings › Meetings help "How the co-pilot works in Demo Studio’s meetings…"; Reports tile "0 of 12 with the co-pilot on"; Tools tile "Meeting Copilot".
findings.why: A product name spelled four ways looks careless in a demo.
findings.proposal: One spelling: "Meeting Copilot" as the name, "Copilot" in a sentence ("with Copilot on").

findings.title: Member rows don't line up; Marketing / Accounting rows flip actions to the left
findings.now: The second line's controls shift with their content (Hui Min's "Projects at once" select is pushed right by the "CLOSED TO NEW LEADS" chip); Nurul Huda (Marketing) and Priya Tan (Accounting) show "Add PayNow · Public profile · Deactivate" left-aligned under the name while every other row's actions are right-aligned; the preference summary is cut to "Land…" / "Cond…" / "HDB & BTO homes, c…".
findings.why: A ragged list reads as broken; the cut preferences hide the one useful fact of that column.
findings.proposal: Solved by the one-row model (first finding). If the row stays, put the second line on a fixed grid and right-align the actions on every role.

themes.title: One vocabulary for the whole app
themes.why: The same thing has up to eight names across modules — the attention list, approvals, money still owed, tickets, members, stages, trades — so a studio owner can't trust that two screens mean the same thing.
themes.rule: Adopt one glossary and use it everywhere: Needs your attention (was Needs you · To do · Needs my review…) · Approvals (was To approve · Needs your OK · Your OK) · Payments for a project's money tab (was Money), with Client payments and Costs inside it and in Finance (was Money in · Money out · Billing) · To collect / To pay / Collected / Paid for money · Issues (was Tickets · Escalations) · Members (never Team · People · Collaborators) · Client (never Homeowner) · Trade (never Category) · Stage only for a lead's or a project's stage. The Words table lists every change.

themes.title: One verb on a row — the rest in its ⋮
themes.why: Rows repeat three to five purple text actions (Members has 28 on one screen, Tasks 63), so the eye can't find the one thing a row is for.
themes.rule: Every list row shows at most one action — the DS secondary text button — and everything else moves into the row's ⋮ (PortalMenu). No 'Open' beside a ⋮: the row itself opens. Hover tools never cover a row's own cells.

themes.title: One filled button per screen
themes.why: Several screens carry two to four filled buttons (the lead page, the project's Money tab, Integrations, the Visualizer editor), and some offer a move the page will refuse.
themes.rule: A screen has at most one filled button, for its one job; it is never a state ('Shared with client') and never a move the page knows it will refuse. Everything else is outlined or text.

themes.title: Say each thing once
themes.why: The same fact or next step is printed three to five times on one page (a project's next step, a lead's dates, X-Ray's difference, a held meeting's concerns).
themes.rule: One fact lives in one place on a screen: the header's next step is not repeated in a card, a banner and a row; a tag never repeats the heading or the status pill next to it.

themes.title: Explanations off the page
themes.why: Paragraphs and 'how it works' boxes sit on every visit (Members' five lines, every Settings module's signposts, 3,000–5,000 px help-heavy pages, prototype disclaimers on studio screens).
themes.rule: A screen says what it is in one line. Longer help goes behind a 'How this works' link or the house Tooltip, and a tool's how-it-works shows on the first visit only. Prototype / demo talk never sits on a studio's screen.

themes.title: Capitals only for a status
themes.why: CAPITAL tags carry dates, counts, names, topics and property types ('29 SEP ’26', 'HDB 4-ROOM', 'MANDATORY' on 34 of 38 rows), so a real status no longer stands out.
themes.rule: Uppercase is kept for status tags only (Draft, Sent, Overdue …). Meta (a date, a type, a count, a name) is sentence-case secondary text; card heads are one style — bold sentence case.

themes.title: Counts only where they help — one way to write them
themes.why: Numbers sit on every chip and tab (Marketplace shows 11 on its first screen), are written five ways ('Needs you 51', 'Overdue · 6', '(48)', 'Open (3)', '4 to approve'), and the rail wears six red badges at rest.
themes.rule: A count shows only where it changes a decision (what waits on you); it is written one way ('Label · n'); a red badge means overdue-and-yours only, everything else is a quiet count or nothing.

themes.title: Empty means quiet
themes.why: Columns of '--', 'Not set', 'No preferences set', 'Nothing yet' run down lists and info columns, written three ways ('--', '- -', '—').
themes.rule: An empty value shows nothing (the row is left out, or the field reads as an Add affordance once). Where a dash must stand in a table cell, it is one style: '—'.

themes.title: Plain words a studio owner says
themes.why: Rows and labels read like system events, statistics or rule engines ('OM-10008’s price ended … while Vivien has it', 'Creation → Assignment 26.3h median', 'Studio default · 4', 'Runs the studio').
themes.rule: Every title, label and status is a sentence a studio owner would say out loud; no field codes, no medians, no internal names; verbs say what happens. Each rewrite is in the Words table.

themes.title: One look for each kind of control
themes.why: The same job is drawn several ways: views and filters as text tabs, segmented controls, outlined and bordered chips; 'create' as eleven different verbs and looks; three ways to save; two Preview bars.
themes.rule: One house piece per job: Tabs to switch a view, the scope pill + Filters to narrow a list, one create button ('New …' + ▾) in one place, autosave (or one Save) on settings pages, one card head, one Preview bar.

themes.title: One format for dates, money and time
themes.why: Six to eight date styles in one module; the same amount shows as 'S$ 13,370' and 'S$13,370.04'; one meeting shows two different times.
themes.rule: Dates: '24 Oct' this year, '24 Oct ’25' otherwise, 'today · yesterday · tomorrow' near now; money: 'S$ 13,370' on cards and tiles, 'S$13,370.04' only on documents; the house clock '2:00 PM'.

themes.title: Never cut the fact that matters
themes.why: Truncation hides the key fact (Company panel help lines, the deal on a Marketplace card, a task's title, Finance's 'What to know').
themes.rule: Text that a decision rests on wraps to a second line instead of '…'; only names in a dense table may truncate, with the full words in the house tooltip.

themes.title: Sentence case everywhere
themes.why: Buttons, menus and column names mix Title Case and sentence case on the same menu ('Add Task' beside 'New ticket', 'Contact Log' beside 'Contact log').
themes.rule: Sentence case for every button, menu row, column, heading and tab; proper names keep their capitals.

themes.title: Long pages fold
themes.why: Some pages draw everything open: a 120-row permission matrix (8,123 px), 232 message previews (26,324 px), seven report tables half of them empty, a 51-row inbox unrolled in its card, 17-row menus.
themes.rule: A page shows the summary and the first few rows; the rest folds behind 'Show all n' or opens in a drawer; menus stay under ten rows (group or split them); an empty table is one line, not a table.

themes.title: Phones get designed cards and a useful first screen
themes.why: On a phone, Finance lists are tables turned sideways (seven label lines a card), chips lose their words, every card has its own ⋮ and verb line, and the first screen is the header and the AI brief.
themes.rule: Every list on a phone uses the Leads card model (two lines + one action); chips keep their words; the first screen shows what needs doing; the Maison AI button never covers a row.

themes.title: One home per place, named plainly
themes.why: Tools mixes the studio's Quotes and Contracts with AI tools and has two 3D tools; 'Qanvast Ops' reads as Qanvast's console; Finance and Reports hide in Company; the rail and the phone dock order things differently.
themes.rule: Name and place each module where a studio owner looks for it: the daily work on the rail in one order everywhere, the AI tools in Tools, the studio's Qanvast account named as such; settings live in one place (Settings vs Company split decided once).

themes.title: Numbers and states that disagree
themes.why: Some screens contradict each other: three counts for the same approvals, an amount that differs between a row and its pane, two different 'Profit' figures a tab apart, a portal card saying 'under way' above one saying 'paused', a contract's date 13 days off its record.
themes.rule: One number for one fact, read from one place (the Dashboard's D5 rule applied across modules); a state is written once and shown the same everywhere.

themes.title: Defects to fix whatever else is decided
themes.why: Things that are simply broken: text squeezed into a few words a line at 1440, Esc taking you off the lead, a ghost that doesn’t match its page, rows that don’t line up, notification previews that all link to a lead.
themes.rule: Fix each where it is; none needs a design call.
